3.15.s:
tacchrutvā vacanaṃ devī mandasmitamukhāṃbujā /
uvāca sa tato vākyaṃ brahmaviṣṇumukhānsurān //
3.15.d:
तच्छ्रुत्वा वचनं देवी मन्दस्मितमुखांबुजा ।
उवाच स ततो वाक्यं ब्रह्मविष्णुमुखान्सुरान् ॥
3.15.m: Hearing those words, the goddess, whose lotus face bore a gentle smile, / then spoke these words to the gods headed by Brahmā and Viṣṇu:

3.15.s:
svatantrāhaṃ sadā devāḥ svecchācāravihāriṇī /
mamānurūpacarito bhavitā tu mama priyaḥ //
3.15.d:
स्वतन्त्राहं सदा देवाः स्वेच्छाचारविहारिणी ।
ममानुरूपचरितो भविता तु मम प्रियः ॥
3.15.m: “I am ever independent, O gods, roaming according to my own will; / but he whose conduct conforms to mine shall be my beloved.”

3.15.s:
tatheti tatpratiśrutya sarverdevaiḥ pitāmahaḥ /
uvāca ca mahādevīṃ dharmārthasahitaṃ vacaḥ //
3.15.d:
तथेति तत्प्रतिश्रुत्य सर्वेर्देवैः पितामहः ।
उवाच च महादेवीं धर्मार्थसहितं वचः ॥
3.15.m: Promising “So be it” along with all the gods, the grandfather / spoke words endowed with righteousness and purpose to the great goddess:

3.15.s:
kālakrītā krayakrītā pitṛdattā svayaṃyutā /
nārīpuruṣayorevamudvāhastu caturvidhaḥ //
3.15.d:
कालक्रीता क्रयक्रीता पितृदत्ता स्वयंयुता ।
नारीपुरुषयोरेवमुद्वाहस्तु चतुर्विधः ॥
3.15.m: “Purchased by time, purchased by price, given by the father, or united by self-choice: / such is the fourfold marriage between woman and man.

3.15.s:
kālakrītā tu veśyā syātkrayakrītā tu dāsikā /
gandharvodvāhitā yuktā bhāryā syātpitṛdattakā //
3.15.d:
कालक्रीता तु वेश्या स्यात्क्रयक्रीता तु दासिका ।
गन्धर्वोद्वाहिता युक्ता भार्या स्यात्पितृदत्तका ॥
3.15.m: One purchased by time would be a courtesan; one purchased by price is a handmaid; / a wife married by the gandharva rite is appropriate, as is one given by the father.

3.15.s:
samānadharmiṇī yuktā bhāryā pitṛvaśaṃvadā /
yadadvaitaṃ paraṃ brahma sadasadbhāvavarjitam //
3.15.d:
समानधर्मिणी युक्ता भार्या पितृवशंवदा ।
यदद्वैतं परं ब्रह्म सदसद्भाववर्जितम् ॥
3.15.m: A wife of equal duty, obedient to her father, is appropriate. / That non-dual, supreme Brahman, devoid of the states of existence and non-existence,

3.15.s:
cidānandātmakaṃ tasmātprakṛtiḥ samajāyata /
tvamevāsīcca tadbrahma prakṛtiḥ sā tvameva hi //
3.15.d:
चिदानन्दात्मकं तस्मात्प्रकृतिः समजायत ।
त्वमेवासीच्च तद्ब्रह्म प्रकृतिः सा त्वमेव हि ॥
3.15.m: Consisting of consciousness and bliss—from that, Prakṛti was born. / You alone were that Brahman, and you alone indeed are that Prakṛti.

3.15.s:
tvamevānādirakhilā kāryakāraṇarūpiṇī /
tvāmeva hi vicinvanti yoginaḥ sanakādayaḥ //
3.15.d:
त्वमेवानादिरखिला कार्यकारणरूपिणी ।
त्वामेव हि विचिन्वन्ति योगिनः सनकादयः ॥
3.15.m: You alone are beginningless, the whole, having the nature of cause and effect; / you alone indeed do the yogins headed by Sanaka seek out.

3.15.s:
sadasatkarmarūpāṃ ca vyaktāvyakto dayātmikām /
tvāmeva hi praśaṃsaṃti pañcabrahmasvarūpiṇīm //
3.15.d:
सदसत्कर्मरूपां च व्यक्ताव्यक्तो दयात्मिकाम् ।
त्वामेव हि प्रशंसंति पञ्चब्रह्मस्वरूपिणीम् ॥
3.15.m: Having the form of good and bad deeds, consisting of the rise of manifest and unmanifest, / you alone do they praise as the embodiment of the five Brahmans.

3.15.s:
tvāmeva hi sṛjasyādau tvameva hyavasi kṣaṇāt /
bhajasva puruṣaṃ kañcillokānugrahakāmyayā //
3.15.d:
त्वामेव हि सृजस्यादौ त्वमेव ह्यवसि क्षणात् ।
भजस्व पुरुषं कञ्चिल्लोकानुग्रहकाम्यया ॥
3.15.m: You alone create in the beginning, and you alone protect in an instant; / betake yourself to a consort out of a desire to show grace to the worlds.”

3.15.s:
iti vijñāpitā devī brahmaṇā sakalaiḥ suraiḥ /
srajamudyamya hastena cakṣepa gaganāntare //
3.15.d:
इति विज्ञापिता देवी ब्रह्मणा सकलैः सुरैः ।
स्रजमुद्यम्य हस्तेन चक्षेप गगनान्तरे ॥
3.15.m: Thus petitioned by Brahmā and all the gods, the goddess / raised a garland with her hand and cast it into the mid-sky.

3.15.s:
tayotsṛṣṭā hi sā mālā śobhayantī nabhasthalam /
papāta kaṇṭhadeśe hi tadā kāmeśvarasya tu //
3.15.d:
तयोत्सृष्टा हि सा माला शोभयन्ती नभस्थलम् ।
पपात कण्ठदेशे हि तदा कामेश्वरस्य तु ॥
3.15.m: Thrown by her, that garland, illuminating the firmament, / fell then around the neck of Kāmeśvara.

3.15.s:
tato mumudire devā brahmaviṣṇupurogamāḥ /
vavṛṣuḥ puṣpavarṣāṇi mandavāteritā ghanāḥ //
3.15.d:
ततो मुमुदिरे देवा ब्रह्मविष्णुपुरोगमाः ।
ववृषुः पुष्पवर्षाणि मन्दवातेरिता घनाः ॥
3.15.m: Then the gods headed by Brahmā and Viṣṇu rejoiced; / clouds stirred by gentle breezes poured down showers of flowers.

3.15.s:
athovāca vidhātā tu bhagavantaṃ janārdanam /
kartavyo vidhinodvāhastvanayoḥ śivayorhare //
3.15.d:
अथोवाच विधाता तु भगवन्तं जनार्दनम् ।
कर्तव्यो विधिनोद्वाहस्त्वनयोः शिवयोर्हरे ॥
3.15.m: Then the Creator spoke to the venerable Janārdana: / “The marriage of these two auspicious deities must be performed according to the prescribed rite, O Hari.

3.15.s:
muhurto devasamprāpto jaganmaṅgalakārakaḥ /
tvadrūpā hi mahādevī sahajaśca bhavānapi //
3.15.d:
मुहुर्तो देवसम्प्राप्तो जगन्मङ्गलकारकः ।
त्वद्रूपा हि महादेवी सहजश्च भवानपि ॥
3.15.m: The auspicious moment that brings welfare to the world has arrived, O god; / for the great goddess is your own form, and you are her brother.

3.15.s:
dātumarhasi kalyāṇīmasmai kāmaśivāya tu /
tacchrutvā vacanaṃ tasya devadevastrivikramaḥ //
3.15.d:
दातुमर्हसि कल्याणीमस्मै कामशिवाय तु ।
तच्छ्रुत्वा वचनं तस्य देवदेवस्त्रिविक्रमः ॥
3.15.m: You ought to give this auspicious lady to this Kāmaśiva.” / Hearing his words, Trivikrama, god of gods,

3.15.s:
dadau tasyai vidhānena prītyā tāṃ śaṅkarāya tu /
devarṣipitṛmukhyānāṃ sarveṣāṃ devayoginām //
3.15.d:
ददौ तस्यै विधानेन प्रीत्या तां शङ्कराय तु ।
देवर्षिपितृमुख्यानां सर्वेषां देवयोगिनाम् ॥
3.15.m: Gave her in accordance with the rite and with affection to Śaṅkara, / in the presence of the foremost divine sages, ancestors, and all divine yogins.

3.15.s:
kalyāṇaṃ kārayāmāsa śivayorādikeśavaḥ /
upāyanāni pradaduḥ sarve brahmādayaḥ surāḥ //
3.15.d:
कल्याणं कारयामास शिवयोरादिकेशवः ।
उपायनानि प्रददुः सर्वे ब्रह्मादयः सुराः ॥
3.15.m: Primeval Keśava had the wedding of Śiva and Śivā performed. / All the gods, beginning with Brahmā, presented gifts.

3.15.s:
dadau brahmekṣucāpaṃ tu vajrasāramanaśvaram /
tayoḥ puṣpāyudhaṃ prādādamlānaṃ hariravyayam //
3.15.d:
ददौ ब्रह्मेक्षुचापं तु वज्रसारमनश्वरम् ।
तयोः पुष्पायुधं प्रादादम्लानं हरिरव्ययम् ॥
3.15.m: Brahmā gave a sugarcane bow, hard as a diamond and imperishable; / to the two of them Hari gave an unfading, imperishable weapon of flowers.

3.15.s:
nāgapāśaṃ dadau tābhyāṃ varuṇo yādasāṃpatiḥ /
aṅkuśaṃ ca dadau tābhyāṃ viśvakarmā viśāṃpatiḥ //
3.15.d:
नागपाशं ददौ ताभ्यां वरुणो यादसांपतिः ।
अङ्कुशं च ददौ ताभ्यां विश्वकर्मा विशांपतिः ॥
3.15.m: Varuṇa, lord of aquatic creatures, gave them a serpent-noose; / and Viśvakarmā, master of men, gave them a goad.

3.15.s:
kirīṭamagniḥ prāyacchattāṭaṅkau candrabhāskarau /
navaratnamayīṃ bhūṣāṃ prādādratnākaraḥ svayam //
3.15.d:
किरीटमग्निः प्रायच्छत्ताटङ्कौ चन्द्रभास्करौ ।
नवरत्नमयीं भूषां प्रादाद्रत्नाकरः स्वयम् ॥
3.15.m: Agni gave a diadem; the moon and the sun [gave] two earrings; / the ocean itself gave an ornament made of the nine jewels.

3.15.s:
dadau surāṇāmadhipo madhupātramathākṣayam /
cintāmaṇimayīṃ mālāṃ kuberaḥ pradadau tadā //
3.15.d:
ददौ सुराणामधिपो मधुपात्रमथाक्षयम् ।
चिन्तामणिमयीं मालां कुबेरः प्रददौ तदा ॥
3.15.m: Then the ruler of the gods gave an inexhaustible honey-vessel; / Kubera then presented a garland made of cintāmaṇi stones.

3.15.s:
sāmrājyasūcakaṃ chatraṃ dadau lakṣmīpatiḥ svayam /
gaṅgā ca yamunā tābhyāṃ cāmare candrabhāsvare //
3.15.d:
साम्राज्यसूचकं छत्रं ददौ लक्ष्मीपतिः स्वयम् ।
गङ्गा च यमुना ताभ्यां चामरे चन्द्रभास्वरे ॥
3.15.m: The husband of Lakṣmī himself gave an umbrella indicating universal sovereignty; / and Gaṅgā and Yamunā [gave] them two flywhisks radiant as the moon.

3.15.s:
aṣṭau ca vasavo rudrā ādityāścāśvinau tathā /
dikpālā marutaḥ sādhyā gandharvāḥ pramatheśvarāḥ /
svānisvānyāyudhānyasyai pradaduḥ paritoṣitāḥ //
3.15.d:
अष्टौ च वसवो रुद्रा आदित्याश्चाश्विनौ तथा ।
दिक्पाला मरुतः साध्या गन्धर्वाः प्रमथेश्वराः ।
स्वानिस्वान्यायुधान्यस्यै प्रददुः परितोषिताः ॥
3.15.m: The eight Vasus, the Rudras, the Ādityas, and the two Aśvins, / the guardians of the quarters, the Maruts, the Sādhyas, the Gandharvas, and the lords of the Pramathas, / being fully gratified, presented each their own weapons to her.

3.15.s:
rathāṃśca turagānnāgānmahāvegānmahābalān /
uṣṭānarogānaśvāṃstānkṣuttṛṣṇāparivarjitān /
dadurvajropamākārānsāyudhānsaparicchadān //
3.15.d:
रथांश्च तुरगान्नागान्महावेगान्महाबलान् ।
उष्टानरोगानश्वांस्तान्क्षुत्तृष्णापरिवर्जितान् ।
ददुर्वज्रोपमाकारान्सायुधान्सपरिच्छदान् ॥
3.15.m: Chariots, horses, elephants of great speed and great strength, / camels, healthy horses free from hunger and thirst, / shaped like thunderbolts, with weapons and equipment, they gave [her].

3.15.s:
athābhiṣekamātenuḥ sāmrājye śivayoḥ śivam /
athākarodvimānaṃ ca nāmnā tu kusumākaram //
3.15.d:
अथाभिषेकमातेनुः साम्राज्ये शिवयोः शिवम् ।
अथाकरोद्विमानं च नाम्ना तु कुसुमाकरम् ॥
3.15.m: Then they performed the auspicious consecration into imperial rule for Śiva and Śivā. / Then the Creator fashioned a celestial chariot named Kusumākara,

3.15.s:
vidhātāmlānamālaṃ vai nityaṃ cābhedyamāyudhaiḥ /
divi bhuvyantarikṣe ca kāmagaṃ susamṛddhimat //
3.15.d:
विधाताम्लानमालं वै नित्यं चाभेद्यमायुधैः ।
दिवि भुव्यन्तरिक्षे च कामगं सुसमृद्धिमत् ॥
3.15.m: verily with unfading garlands, and forever impenetrable by weapons, / moving at will in heaven, on earth, and in the atmosphere, richly abundant,

3.15.s:
yadgandhaghrāṇamātreṇa bhrāntirogakṣurdhātayaḥ /
tatkṣaṇādeva naśyanti manohlādakaraṃ śubham //
3.15.d:
यद्गन्धघ्राणमात्रेण भ्रान्तिरोगक्षुर्धातयः ।
तत्क्षणादेव नश्यन्ति मनोह्लादकरं शुभम् ॥
3.15.m: by merely smelling whose fragrance delusions, diseases, hunger, and thirst / are destroyed that very instant; delighting the mind and auspicious.

3.15.s:
tadvimānamathāropya tāvubhau divyadaṃpatī /
cāmakhyājanacchatradhvajayaṣṭimanoharam //
3.15.d:
तद्विमानमथारोप्य तावुभौ दिव्यदंपती ।
चामख्याजनच्छत्रध्वजयष्टिमनोहरम् ॥
3.15.m: Then, having mounted that celestial chariot— / enchanting with flywhisks, fans, umbrellas, and flagstaffs—those two divine spouses,

3.15.s:
vīṇāveṇumṛdaṅgādivividhaistauryavādanaiḥ /
sevyamānā suragaṇairnirgatya nṛpamandirāt //
3.15.d:
वीणावेणुमृदङ्गादिविविधैस्तौर्यवादनैः ।
सेव्यमाना सुरगणैर्निर्गत्य नृपमन्दिरात् ॥
3.15.m: being attended upon by the hosts of gods with various musical performances / of vīṇās, flutes, mṛdaṅgas, and the like, went forth from the royal palace.

3.15.s:
yayau vīthīṃ vihāreśā śobhayantī nijaujasā /
pratiharmyāgrasaṃsthābhirapsarobhiḥ sahasraśaḥ //
3.15.d:
ययौ वीथीं विहारेशा शोभयन्ती निजौजसा ।
प्रतिहर्म्याग्रसंस्थाभिरप्सरोभिः सहस्रशः ॥
3.15.m: The sovereign mistress of delight went along the street, adorning it with her own splendour. / By thousands of apsarases stationed on the roofs of every mansion,

3.15.s:
salājākṣatahastābhiḥ purandhrībhiśca varṣitā /
gāthābhirmaṅgalārthābhirvīṇāveṇvādinisvanaiḥ /
tuṣyantī vīvīthivīthīṣu mandamandamathāyayau //
3.15.d:
सलाजाक्षतहस्ताभिः पुरन्ध्रीभिश्च वर्षिता ।
गाथाभिर्मङ्गलार्थाभिर्वीणावेण्वादिनिस्वनैः ।
तुष्यन्ती वीवीथिवीथीषु मन्दमन्दमथाययौ ॥
3.15.m: and by married women holding parched grain and unbroken rice in their hands, showered [with auspicious items], / being delighted with songs of auspicious import and sounds of vīṇās, flutes, and the like, she then proceeded very slowly through the various streets.

3.15.s:
pratigṛhyāpsa robhistu kṛtaṃ nīrājanāvidhim /
avaruhya vimānagrātpraviveśa mahāsabhām //
3.15.d:
प्रतिगृह्याप्स रोभिस्तु कृतं नीराजनाविधिम् ।
अवरुह्य विमानग्रात्प्रविवेश महासभाम् ॥
3.15.m: Accepting the ritual of waving lights performed by the apsarases, / having descended from the foremost chariot, she entered the great assembly hall.

3.15.s:
siṃhāsanamadhiṣṭhāya saha devena śaṃbhunā /
yadyadvāñchanti tatrasthā manasaiva mahājanāḥ /
sarvajñā sākṣipātena tattatkāmānapūrayat //
3.15.d:
सिंहासनमधिष्ठाय सह देवेन शंभुना ।
यद्यद्वाञ्छन्ति तत्रस्था मनसैव महाजनाः ।
सर्वज्ञा साक्षिपातेन तत्तत्कामानपूरयत् ॥
3.15.m: Taking her place on the lion-throne together with the god Śambhu, / whatever the great people standing there desired in their minds, / the omniscient one fulfilled those very desires with a mere cast of her eye.

3.15.s:
taddṛṣṭvā caritaṃ devyā brahmā loka pitāmahaḥ /
kāmākṣīti tadābhikhyāṃ dadau kāmeśvarīti ca //
3.15.d:
तद्दृष्ट्वा चरितं देव्या ब्रह्मा लोक पितामहः ।
कामाक्षीति तदाभिख्यां ददौ कामेश्वरीति च ॥
3.15.m: Beholding that deed of the goddess, Brahmā, the grandfather of the worlds, / then gave her the names Kāmākṣī and Kāmeśvarī.

3.15.s:
vavarṣāścaryamegho 'pi pure tasmiṃstadājñayā /
mahārhāṇi ca vastūni divyānyābharaṇāni ca //
3.15.d:
ववर्षाश्चर्यमेघो ऽपि पुरे तस्मिंस्तदाज्ञया ।
महार्हाणि च वस्तूनि दिव्यान्याभरणानि च ॥
3.15.m: A cloud of wonders also rained down upon that city by her command / very precious articles and divine ornaments.

3.15.s:
cintāmaṇiḥ kalpavṛkṣaḥ kamalā kāmadhenavaḥ /
prativeśma tatastasthuḥ puro devyājayāya te //
3.15.d:
चिन्तामणिः कल्पवृक्षः कमला कामधेनवः ।
प्रतिवेश्म ततस्तस्थुः पुरो देव्याजयाय ते ॥
3.15.m: The wish-fulfilling jewel, the wish-granting tree, Lakṣmī, and wish-yielding cows / then stood before every house in the city for the victory of the goddess.

3.15.s:
tāṃ sevaikarasākārāṃ vimuktānyakriyāguṇāḥ /
sarvakāmārthasaṃyuktā hṛṣyantaḥ sārvakālikam //
3.15.d:
तां सेवैकरसाकारां विमुक्तान्यक्रियागुणाः ।
सर्वकामार्थसंयुक्ता हृष्यन्तः सार्वकालिकम् ॥
3.15.m: Having the single essence of serving her, free from the qualities of other actions, / endowed with all desired objects, rejoicing at all times,

3.15.s:
pitāmaho hariścaiva mahādevaśca vāsavaḥ /
anye diśāmadhīśāstu sakalā devatāgaṇāḥ //
3.15.d:
पितामहो हरिश्चैव महादेवश्च वासवः ।
अन्ये दिशामधीशास्तु सकला देवतागणाः ॥
3.15.m: the Grandfather, Hari, Mahādeva, Indra, / the other rulers of the directions, and all the hosts of deities,

3.15.s:
devarṣayo nāradādyāḥ sanakādyāśca yoginaḥ /
maharṣayaśca manvādyā vaśiṣṭhādyāstapodhanāḥ //
3.15.d:
देवर्षयो नारदाद्याः सनकाद्याश्च योगिनः ।
महर्षयश्च मन्वाद्या वशिष्ठाद्यास्तपोधनाः ॥
3.15.m: the divine seers beginning with Nārada, the yogins beginning with Sanaka, / the great seers beginning with Manu, and those rich in asceticism beginning with Vasiṣṭha,

3.15.s:
gandharvāpsaraso yakṣā yāścānyā devajātayaḥ /
divi bhūmyantarikṣeṣu sasaṃbādhaṃ vasaṃti ye //
3.15.d:
गन्धर्वाप्सरसो यक्षा याश्चान्या देवजातयः ।
दिवि भूम्यन्तरिक्षेषु ससंबाधं वसंति ये ॥
3.15.m: Gandharvas, apsarases, Yakṣas, and whatever other classes of deities / dwell crowded together in heaven, on earth, and in the atmosphere—

3.15.s: te sarve cāpyasaṃbādhaṃ nivasaṃti sma tatpure //
3.15.d: ते सर्वे चाप्यसंबाधं निवसंति स्म तत्पुरे ॥
3.15.m: all of them dwelt uncrowded in that city.

3.15.s:
evaṃ tadvatsalā devī nānyatraityakhilājjanāt /
toṣayāmāsa satatamanurāgeṇa bhūyasā //
3.15.d:
एवं तद्वत्सला देवी नान्यत्रैत्यखिलाज्जनात् ।
तोषयामास सततमनुरागेण भूयसा ॥
3.15.m: In this way, that affectionate goddess, never departing elsewhere from all the people, / constantly satisfied them with great love.

3.15.s:
rājño mahati bhūrloke viduṣaḥ sakalepsitām /
rājñī dudohābhīṣṭāni sarvabhūtalavāsinām //
3.15.d:
राज्ञो महति भूर्लोके विदुषः सकलेप्सिताम् ।
राज्ञी दुदोहाभीष्टानि सर्वभूतलवासिनाम् ॥
3.15.m: The queen milked all desired wishes for the wise king on the great earthly realm, / [and fulfilled] the desires of all beings living on the earth.

3.15.s:
trilokaikamahīpāle sāṃbike kāmaśaṅkare /
daśavarṣasahasrāṇi yayuḥ kṣaṇa ivāparaḥ //
3.15.d:
त्रिलोकैकमहीपाले सांबिके कामशङ्करे ।
दशवर्षसहस्राणि ययुः क्षण इवापरः ॥
3.15.m: While the auspicious Kāmaśaṅkara, accompanied by Ambikā, was the sole monarch of the three worlds, / ten thousand years passed away like another single instant.

3.15.s:
tataḥ kadā cidāgatya nārado bhagavānṛṣiḥ /
praṇamya paramāṃ śaktiṃ provāca vinayānvitaḥ //
3.15.d:
ततः कदा चिदागत्य नारदो भगवानृषिः ।
प्रणम्य परमां शक्तिं प्रोवाच विनयान्वितः ॥
3.15.m: Then, once upon a time, the blessed seer Nārada arrived, / bowed to the supreme Power, and said with modesty:

3.15.s:
para brahma paraṃ dhāma pavitraṃ paramaiśvari /
madasadbhāvasaṃkalpavikalpakalanātmikā //
3.15.d:
पर ब्रह्म परं धाम पवित्रं परमैश्वरि ।
मदसद्भावसंकल्पविकल्पकलनात्मिका ॥
3.15.m: "O supreme Brahman! O supreme abode! O pure one! O supreme ruler! / O you whose nature is the ideation of existence and non-existence, of determination and doubt!

3.15.s:
jagadabhyudayārthāya vyaktabhāvamupāgatā /
asajjanavināśārthā sajjanābhyudayārthinī /
pravṛttistava kalyāṇi sādhūnāṃ rakṣaṇāya hi //
3.15.d:
जगदभ्युदयार्थाय व्यक्तभावमुपागता ।
असज्जनविनाशार्था सज्जनाभ्युदयार्थिनी ।
प्रवृत्तिस्तव कल्याणि साधूनां रक्षणाय हि ॥
3.15.m: For the welfare of the world you have assumed an embodied state. / Your activity is for the destruction of the wicked and aims at the welfare of the righteous, / indeed for the protection of the virtuous, O auspicious one!

3.15.s:
ayaṃ bhaṇḍo 'suro devi bādhate jagatāṃ trayam /
tvayaikayaiva jetavyo na śakyastvaparaiḥ suraiḥ //
3.15.d:
अयं भण्डो ऽसुरो देवि बाधते जगतां त्रयम् ।
त्वयैकयैव जेतव्यो न शक्यस्त्वपरैः सुरैः ॥
3.15.m: This asura Bhaṇḍa, O goddess, torments the three worlds. / He must be conquered by you alone; he cannot be conquered by the other gods.

3.15.s:
tvatsevaikaparā devāścirakālamihoṣitāḥ /
tvadājñayā gamiṣyanti svānisvāni purāṇi tu //
3.15.d:
त्वत्सेवैकपरा देवाश्चिरकालमिहोषिताः ।
त्वदाज्ञया गमिष्यन्ति स्वानिस्वानि पुराणि तु ॥
3.15.m: The gods, dedicated solely to your service, have resided here for a long time; / by your command they will go to their own respective cities,

3.15.s:
amaṅgalāni śūnyāni samṛddhārthāni saṃtvataḥ /
evaṃ vijñāpitā devī nāradenākhileśvarī /
svasvavāsanivāsāya preṣayāmāsa cāmarān //
3.15.d:
अमङ्गलानि शून्यानि समृद्धार्थानि संत्वतः ।
एवं विज्ञापिता देवी नारदेनाखिलेश्वरी ।
स्वस्ववासनिवासाय प्रेषयामास चामरान् ॥
3.15.m: which are now inauspicious and deserted, so that they may become full of prosperity." / Thus petitioned by Nārada, the supreme sovereign of all / sent forth the immortals to reside in their respective dwellings.

3.15.s:
brahmāṇaṃ ca hariṃ śaṃbhuṃ vāsavādīndiśāṃ patīn /
yathārhaṃ pūjayitvā tu preṣayāmāsa cāṃbikā //
3.15.d:
ब्रह्माणं च हरिं शंभुं वासवादीन्दिशां पतीन् ।
यथार्हं पूजयित्वा तु प्रेषयामास चांबिका ॥
3.15.m: Having honoured Brahmā, Hari, Śambhu, and the guardians of the directions headed by Indra / according to their deserts, Ambikā sent them away.

3.15.s:
aparādhaṃ tatastyaktumapi saṃpreṣitāḥ surāḥ /
svasvāṃśaiḥ śivayoḥ sevāmādipitrorakurvata //
3.15.d:
अपराधं ततस्त्यक्तुमपि संप्रेषिताः सुराः ।
स्वस्वांशैः शिवयोः सेवामादिपित्रोरकुर्वत ॥
3.15.m: Then, to avoid any fault, the gods who had been dismissed / served Śiva and Śivā, the primeval parents, through portions of themselves.

3.15.s:
etadākhyānamāyuṣyaṃ sarvamaṅgalakāraṇam /
āvirbhāvaṃ mahādevyāstasyā rājyābhiṣecanam //
3.15.d:
एतदाख्यानमायुष्यं सर्वमङ्गलकारणम् ।
आविर्भावं महादेव्यास्तस्या राज्याभिषेचनम् ॥
3.15.m: This narrative prolongs life and is the cause of all auspiciousness— / the manifestation of the great goddess and her consecration into sovereignty.

3.15.s:
yaḥ prātarutthito vidvānbhaktiśraddhāsamanvitaḥ /
japeddhanasamṛddhaḥ syātsudhāsaṃmitavāgbhavet //
3.15.d:
यः प्रातरुत्थितो विद्वान्भक्तिश्रद्धासमन्वितः ।
जपेद्धनसमृद्धः स्यात्सुधासंमितवाग्भवेत् ॥
3.15.m: The wise person who, having risen in the morning, endowed with devotion and faith, / recites it, will become rich in wealth, and his speech will be like nectar.

3.15.s:
nāśubhaṃ vidyate tasya paratreha ca dhīmataḥ /
yaśaḥ prāpnoti vipulaṃ samānottamatāmapi //
3.15.d:
नाशुभं विद्यते तस्य परत्रेह च धीमतः ।
यशः प्राप्नोति विपुलं समानोत्तमतामपि ॥
3.15.m: No misfortune exists for that wise person in this world or in the next; / he obtains vast renown, and also equality with the best.

3.15.s:
acalā śrīrbhavetasya śreyaścaiva padepade /
kadācinna bhayaṃ tasya tejasvī vīryavānbhavet //
3.15.d:
अचला श्रीर्भवेतस्य श्रेयश्चैव पदेपदे ।
कदाचिन्न भयं तस्य तेजस्वी वीर्यवान्भवेत् ॥
3.15.m: Unshakeable fortune will be his, and welfare at every step; / fear will never come to him; he will be radiant and heroic.

3.15.s:
tāpatrayavihīnaśca puruṣārthaiśca pūryate /
trisaṃdhyaṃ yo japennityaṃ dhyātvā siṃhāsaneśvarīm //
3.15.d:
तापत्रयविहीनश्च पुरुषार्थैश्च पूर्यते ।
त्रिसंध्यं यो जपेन्नित्यं ध्यात्वा सिंहासनेश्वरीम् ॥
3.15.m: Free from the three kinds of suffering, he is fulfilled with the goals of human life. / He who, meditating on the Queen of the Lion-Throne, recites it constantly at the three junctions of the day,

3.15.s:
ṣaṇmāsānmahatīṃ lakṣmīṃ prāpnuyājjāpakottamaḥ //
iti śrībrahmāṇḍamahāpurāṇe uttarabhāge hayagrīvāgastyasaṃvāde lalitopākhyāne vaivāhikotsavo nāma pañcadaśo 'dhyāyaḥ
3.15.d:
षण्मासान्महतीं लक्ष्मीं प्राप्नुयाज्जापकोत्तमः ॥
इति श्रीब्रह्माण्डमहापुराणे उत्तरभागे हयग्रीवागस्त्यसंवादे ललितोपाख्याने वैवाहिकोत्सवो नाम पञ्चदशो ऽध्यायः
3.15.m:
that best of reciters will obtain great fortune after six months."

Thus ends the fifteenth chapter, named "The Marriage Festival," in the Lalitopākhyāna, in the dialogue between Hayagrīva and Agastya, in the latter section of the glorious Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa.

3.16.s:
atha sā jagatāṃ mātā lalitā parameśvarī /
trailokyakaṇṭakaṃ bhaṇḍaṃ daityaṃ jetuṃ viniryayau //
3.16.d:
अथ सा जगतां माता ललिता परमेश्वरी ।
त्रैलोक्यकण्टकं भण्डं दैत्यं जेतुं विनिर्ययौ ॥
3.16.m: Then Lalitā, the supreme ruler and mother of the worlds, / marched forth to conquer the daitya Bhaṇḍa, the thorn of the three worlds.

3.16.s:
cakāra mardalākārānaṃbhorāśīṃstu sapta te /
prabhūtamarddaladhvānaiḥ pūrayāmāsuraṃbaram //
3.16.d:
चकार मर्दलाकारानंभोराशींस्तु सप्त ते ।
प्रभूतमर्द्दलध्वानैः पूरयामासुरंबरम् ॥
3.16.m: She made the seven oceans assume the forms of mardala drums; / they filled the sky with vast rumblings of drums.

3.16.s:
mṛdaṅgamurajāścaiva paṭaho 'tukulīṅgaṇāḥ /
selukājhallarīrāṅghāhuhukāhuṇḍukāghaṭāḥ //
3.16.d:
मृदङ्गमुरजाश्चैव पटहो ऽतुकुलीङ्गणाः ।
सेलुकाझल्लरीराङ्घाहुहुकाहुण्डुकाघटाः ॥
3.16.m: Mṛdaṅgas and murajas, paṭahas, atukulīṅgaṇas, / selukās, jhallarīs, rāṅghās, huhukās, huṇḍukas, ghaṭas,

3.16.s:
ānakāḥ paṇavāścaiva gomukhāścārdhacandrikāḥ /
yavamadhyā muṣṭimadhyā marddalāḍiṇḍimā api //
3.16.d:
आनकाः पणवाश्चैव गोमुखाश्चार्धचन्द्रिकाः ।
यवमध्या मुष्टिमध्या मर्द्दलाडिण्डिमा अपि ॥
3.16.m: ānakas, paṇavas, gomukhas, ardhacandrikās, / yavamadhyas, muṣṭimadhyas, mardalas, and ḍiṇḍimas [sounded].

3.16.s:
jharjharāśca barītāśca iṅgyāliṅgyaprabhedajāḥ /
uddhakāścaituhuṇḍāśca niḥsāṇā barbarāḥ pare //
3.16.d:
झर्झराश्च बरीताश्च इङ्ग्यालिङ्ग्यप्रभेदजाः ।
उद्धकाश्चैतुहुण्डाश्च निःसाणा बर्बराः परे ॥
3.16.m: Jharjharas, barītas, instruments of the iṅgya and āliṅgya classes, / uddhakas, aituhuṇḍas, niḥsāṇas, and other barbaras,

3.16.s:
huṅkārā kākatuṇḍāśca vādyabhedāstathāpare /
dadhvanuḥ śaktisenābhirāhatāḥ samarodyame //
3.16.d:
हुङ्कारा काकतुण्डाश्च वाद्यभेदास्तथापरे ।
दध्वनुः शक्तिसेनाभिराहताः समरोद्यमे ॥
3.16.m: huṅkāras, kākatuṇḍas, and other kinds of musical instruments / resounded, struck by the armies of the Śaktis in their preparation for battle.

3.16.s:
lalitāparameśānyā aṅkuśāstrānsamudgatā /
saṃpatkarī nāma devī cacāla saha śaktibhiḥ //
3.16.d:
ललितापरमेशान्या अङ्कुशास्त्रान्समुद्गता ।
संपत्करी नाम देवी चचाल सह शक्तिभिः ॥
3.16.m: Arising from the goad-weapon of the supreme sovereign Lalitā, / the goddess named Saṃpatkarī set forth accompanied by the Śaktis.

3.16.s:
anekakoṭimātaṅgaturaṅgarathapaṅktibhiḥ /
sevitā taruṇādityapāṭalā saṃpadīśvarī //
3.16.d:
अनेककोटिमातङ्गतुरङ्गरथपङ्क्तिभिः ।
सेविता तरुणादित्यपाटला संपदीश्वरी ॥
3.16.m: Attended by lines of many millions of elephants, horses, and chariots, / the sovereign goddess of riches shone rosy-red like the newly risen sun.

3.16.s:
mattamuddaṇḍasaṃgrāmarasikaṃ śailasannibham /
raṇakolāhalaṃ nāma sāruroha mataṅgajam //
3.16.d:
मत्तमुद्दण्डसंग्रामरसिकं शैलसन्निभम् ।
रणकोलाहलं नाम सारुरोह मतङ्गजम् ॥
3.16.m: She mounted an elephant named Raṇakolāhala, / like unto a mountain, impassioned, reveling in formidable battle.

3.16.s:
tāmanvagā yayau senā mahatī dhorarāviṇī /
lolābhiḥ ketumālābhirullikhantī dhanādhanāt //
3.16.d:
तामन्वगा ययौ सेना महती धोरराविणी ।
लोलाभिः केतुमालाभिरुल्लिखन्ती धनाधनात् ॥
3.16.m: A vast army, roaring fiercely, followed after her, / grazing the rain clouds with its fluttering rows of banners.

3.16.s:
tasyāśca saṃpannāthāyāḥ pīnastanasusaṃkaṭaḥ /
kaṇṭako ghanasaṃnāho ruruce vakṣasisthitaḥ //
3.16.d:
तस्याश्च संपन्नाथायाः पीनस्तनसुसंकटः ।
कण्टको घनसंनाहो रुरुचे वक्षसिस्थितः ॥
3.16.m: And on the chest of that mistress of riches, tightly fitted over her swelling breasts, / a thorny, thick coat of mail shone resplendent.

3.16.s:
kaṃpamānā khaḍgalatā vyarucattatkare dhṛtā /
kuṭilā kālanāthasya bhṛkuṭīva bhayaṅkarā //
3.16.d:
कंपमाना खड्गलता व्यरुचत्तत्करे धृता ।
कुटिला कालनाथस्य भृकुटीव भयङ्करा ॥
3.16.m: Quivering in her hand, her slender sword gleamed, / fearsome like the curved knit brow of the Lord of Death.

3.16.s:
utpātavātasaṃpātāccalitā iva parvatāḥ /
tāmanvagā yayuḥ koṭisaṃkhyākāḥ kuñjarottamāḥ //
3.16.d:
उत्पातवातसंपाताच्चलिता इव पर्वताः ।
तामन्वगा ययुः कोटिसंख्याकाः कुञ्जरोत्तमाः ॥
3.16.m: Like mountains set in motion by the impact of cataclysmic winds, / millions of supreme elephants followed after her.

3.16.s:
atha śrīlalitādevyā śrīpāśāyudhasaṃbhavā /
atitvaritavikrāntiraśvārūḍhācalatpuraḥ //
3.16.d:
अथ श्रीललितादेव्या श्रीपाशायुधसंभवा ।
अतित्वरितविक्रान्तिरश्वारूढाचलत्पुरः ॥
3.16.m: Then, born from the sacred noose-weapon of the goddess Śrī Lalitā, / Aśvārūḍhā, whose valour is exceedingly swift, advanced in the vanguard.

3.16.s:
tayā saha hayaprāyaṃ sainyaṃ heṣātaraṅgitam /
vyacaratkhurakuddālavidāritamahītalam //
3.16.d:
तया सह हयप्रायं सैन्यं हेषातरङ्गितम् ।
व्यचरत्खुरकुद्दालविदारितमहीतलम् ॥
3.16.m: Together with her, an army composed mostly of horses, billowing with neighing, / tore up the surface of the earth with their spade-like hooves.

3.16.s:
vanāyujāśca kāṃbojāḥ pāradāḥ siṃdhudeśajāḥ /
ṭaṅkaṇāḥ parvatīyāśca pārasīkāstathā pare //
3.16.d:
वनायुजाश्च कांबोजाः पारदाः सिंधुदेशजाः ।
टङ्कणाः पर्वतीयाश्च पारसीकास्तथा परे ॥
3.16.m: Born in Vanāyu, Kāmboja, Pārada, and the land of Sindhu, / from Ṭaṅkaṇa, from the mountains, and others from Pārasīka;

3.16.s:
ajāneyā ghaṭṭadharā daradāḥ kāla vandijāḥ /
vālmīkayāvanodbhūtā gāndharvāścātha ye hayāḥ //
3.16.d:
अजानेया घट्टधरा दरदाः काल वन्दिजाः ।
वाल्मीकयावनोद्भूता गान्धर्वाश्चाथ ये हयाः ॥
3.16.m: Thoroughbreds, Ghaṭṭadharas, Daradas, born in Kālavandi, / born in Vālmīka and Yavana, and those horses from Gandhāra;

3.16.s:
prāgdeśajātāḥ kairātā prāntadeśodbhavāstathā /
vinītāḥ sādhuvoḍhāro veginaḥ sthiracetasaḥ //
3.16.d:
प्राग्देशजाताः कैराता प्रान्तदेशोद्भवास्तथा ।
विनीताः साधुवोढारो वेगिनः स्थिरचेतसः ॥
3.16.m: Born in the eastern land, Kirāta horses, and those born in border regions, / well-trained, carrying their riders well, swift, and steady of mind;

3.16.s:
svāmicittaviśeṣajñā mahāyuddhasahiṣṇavaḥ /
lakṣaṇairbahubhiryuktā jitakrodhā jitaśramāḥ //
3.16.d:
स्वामिचित्तविशेषज्ञा महायुद्धसहिष्णवः ।
लक्षणैर्बहुभिर्युक्ता जितक्रोधा जितश्रमाः ॥
3.16.m: Knowing the particular mind of their master, enduring great battle, / endowed with many auspicious marks, having overcome anger and conquered fatigue;

3.16.s: pañcadhārāsu śakṣaḍhyā vinītāśca plavānvitāḥ //
3.16.d: पञ्चधारासु शक्षढ्या विनीताश्च प्लवान्विताः ॥
3.16.m: Skilled in the five gaits, well-disciplined, and possessing [great] leaps;

3.16.s:
phalaśuktiśriyā yuktāḥ śvetaśuktisamanvitāḥ /
devapadmaṃ devamaṇiṃ devasvastikameva ca //
3.16.d:
फलशुक्तिश्रिया युक्ताः श्वेतशुक्तिसमन्विताः ।
देवपद्मं देवमणिं देवस्वस्तिकमेव च ॥
3.16.m: Endowed with the splendour of the fruit-pearl-oyster, possessing the white pearl-oyster, / having the divine lotus, the divine jewel, and the divine svastika,

3.16.s:
atha svastikaśuktiśca gaḍuraṃ puṣpagaṇḍikām /
etāni śubhalakṣmāṇi jyarājyapradāni ca /
vahanto vātajavanā vājinastāṃ samanvayuḥ //
3.16.d:
अथ स्वस्तिकशुक्तिश्च गडुरं पुष्पगण्डिकाम् ।
एतानि शुभलक्ष्माणि ज्यराज्यप्रदानि च ।
वहन्तो वातजवना वाजिनस्तां समन्वयुः ॥
3.16.m: And the svastika-pearl-oyster, the gaḍura, and the puṣpagaṇḍikā— / bearing these auspicious marks that bestow victory and kingdom, / the swift-as-wind horses followed her.

3.16.s:
aparājitanāmānamatitejasvinaṃ calam /
atyantottuṅgavarṣmāṇaṃ kavikāvilasanmukham //
3.16.d:
अपराजितनामानमतितेजस्विनं चलम् ।
अत्यन्तोत्तुङ्गवर्ष्माणं कविकाविलसन्मुखम् ॥
3.16.m: Upon [a horse] named Aparājita, exceedingly radiant, restless, / of immensely lofty stature, whose mouth shone with the bit,

3.16.s:
pārśvadvaye 'pi patitasphuratkesaramaṇḍalam /
sthūlavāladhivikṣepakṣipyamāṇapayodharam //
3.16.d:
पार्श्वद्वये ऽपि पतितस्फुरत्केसरमण्डलम् ।
स्थूलवालधिविक्षेपक्षिप्यमाणपयोधरम् ॥
3.16.m: Whose quivering circle of mane fell upon both flanks, / who tossed clouds aside with the sweep of his thick tail,

3.16.s:
jaṅghākāṇḍasamunnaddhamaṇikiṅkiṇibhāsuram /
vādayantamivoccaṇḍaiḥ khuraniṣṭhurakuṭṭanaiḥ //
3.16.d:
जङ्घाकाण्डसमुन्नद्धमणिकिङ्किणिभासुरम् ।
वादयन्तमिवोच्चण्डैः खुरनिष्ठुरकुट्टनैः ॥
3.16.m: Radiant with jewelled small bells bound to his shanks, / who seemed to play, with the fierce pounding of his hooves,

3.16.s:
bhūmaṇḍalamahāvādyaṃ vijayasya samṛddhaye /
ghoṣamāṇaṃ prati muhuḥ saṃdarśitagatikramam //
3.16.d:
भूमण्डलमहावाद्यं विजयस्य समृद्धये ।
घोषमाणं प्रति मुहुः संदर्शितगतिक्रमम् ॥
3.16.m: A great instrument upon the orb of the earth for the increase of victory, / repeatedly displaying the sequence of his paces as he sounded,

3.16.s:
ālolacāmaravyājādvahantaṃ pakṣatī iva /
bhāṇḍairmanoharairyuktaṃ ghargharījālamaṇḍitam //
3.16.d:
आलोलचामरव्याजाद्वहन्तं पक्षती इव ।
भाण्डैर्मनोहरैर्युक्तं घर्घरीजालमण्डितम् ॥
3.16.m: Seeming to bear two wings under the guise of waving chowries, / adorned with charming trappings and embellished with a web of tiny jingling bells—

3.16.s:
eṣāṃ ghoṣasya kapaṭāddhuṅkurvatīmi vāsurān /
aśvārūḍhā mahādevī samārūḍhā hayaṃ yayau //
3.16.d:
एषां घोषस्य कपटाद्धुङ्कुर्वतीमि वासुरान् ।
अश्वारूढा महादेवी समारूढा हयं ययौ ॥
3.16.m: Upon this horse, who seemed to shout in defiance at the Asuras through the guise of his neighing, / the great goddess Aśvārūḍhā mounted and advanced.

3.16.s:
caturbhirvāhubhiḥ pāśamaṅkuśaṃ vetrameva ca /
hayavalgāṃ ca dadhatī bahuvikramaśobhinī //
3.16.d:
चतुर्भिर्वाहुभिः पाशमङ्कुशं वेत्रमेव च ।
हयवल्गां च दधती बहुविक्रमशोभिनी ॥
3.16.m: Holding with her four arms the noose, the goad, the cane, / and the horse's reins, shining with great prowess,

3.16.s:
taruṇādityasaṅkāśā jvalatkāñcītaraṅgiṇī /
sañcacāla hayārūḍhā nartayantīva vājinam //
3.16.d:
तरुणादित्यसङ्काशा ज्वलत्काञ्चीतरङ्गिणी ।
सञ्चचाल हयारूढा नर्तयन्तीव वाजिनम् ॥
3.16.m: Resembling the morning sun, her radiant girdle billowing, / she rode mounted on her horse, as if making her steed dance.

3.16.s:
atha śrīdaṇḍanāthāyā niryāṇapaṭahadhvaniḥ /
uddaṇḍasindhunisvānaścakāra badhiraṃ jagat //
3.16.d:
अथ श्रीदण्डनाथाया निर्याणपटहध्वनिः ।
उद्दण्डसिन्धुनिस्वानश्चकार बधिरं जगत् ॥
3.16.m: Then the sound of the departure-kettledrum of Śrī Daṇḍanāthā, / loud as the roaring ocean, deafened the world.

3.16.s:
vajrabāṇaiḥ kaṭhoraiścabhindantyaḥ kakubho daśa /
anyuddhatabhujāśmānaḥ śaktayaḥ kāściducchritāḥ //
3.16.d:
वज्रबाणैः कठोरैश्चभिन्दन्त्यः ककुभो दश ।
अन्युद्धतभुजाश्मानः शक्तयः काश्चिदुच्छ्रिताः ॥
3.16.m: Splitting the ten directions with hard thunderbolt-arrows, / certain exalted Śaktis advanced with raised stone-like arms.

3.16.s:
kāścicchrīdaṇḍanāthāyāḥ senānāsīrasaṅgatāḥ /
khaḍgaṃ phalakamādāya pupluvuścaṇḍasaktayaḥ //
3.16.d:
काश्चिच्छ्रीदण्डनाथायाः सेनानासीरसङ्गताः ।
खड्गं फलकमादाय पुप्लुवुश्चण्डसक्तयः ॥
3.16.m: Certain fierce Śaktis, joining the vanguard of Śrī Daṇḍanāthā's army, / leaped forward taking up sword and shield.

3.16.s:
atyantasainyasambādhaṃ vetrasaṃtāḍanaiḥ śataiḥ /
nivārayantyo vetriṇyo vyucchalanti smaśaktayaḥ //
3.16.d:
अत्यन्तसैन्यसम्बाधं वेत्रसंताडनैः शतैः ।
निवारयन्त्यो वेत्रिण्यो व्युच्छलन्ति स्मशक्तयः ॥
3.16.m: The cane-bearing Śaktis bounded forth, / warding off the intense crush of the army with hundreds of blows of their canes.

3.16.s:
atha tuṅgadhvajaśreṇīrmahiṣāṅkā mṛgāṅkikām /
sihāṅkāścaiva bibhrāṇāḥ śaktayo vyacalanpurā //
3.16.d:
अथ तुङ्गध्वजश्रेणीर्महिषाङ्का मृगाङ्किकाम् ।
सिहाङ्काश्चैव बिभ्राणाः शक्तयो व्यचलन्पुरा ॥
3.16.m: Then, bearing rows of tall banners emblazoned with the buffalo, the deer, / and the lion, the Śaktis marched in front.

3.16.s:
tataḥ śrīdaṇḍanāthāyāḥ śvetacchatraṃ sahasraśaḥ /
sphuratkarāḥ pracalitāḥ śaktayaḥ kāścidādaduḥ //
iti śrībrahmāṇḍe mahāpurāṇe uttarabhāge hayagrīvāgastyasaṃvāde lalitopākhyāne sasenavijayayātrā nāma ṣoḍaśo 'dhyāyaḥ
3.16.d:
ततः श्रीदण्डनाथायाः श्वेतच्छत्रं सहस्रशः ।
स्फुरत्कराः प्रचलिताः शक्तयः काश्चिदाददुः ॥
इति श्रीब्रह्माण्डे महापुराणे उत्तरभागे हयग्रीवागस्त्यसंवादे ललितोपाख्याने ससेनविजययात्रा नाम षोडशो ऽध्यायः
3.16.m:
Thereupon, thousands of Śaktis, hands flashing, / set forth carrying white umbrellas for Śrī Daṇḍanāthā.

Thus ends the sixteenth chapter, named 'The Triumphal March with the Army', in the Lalitopākhyāna, in the dialogue between Hayagrīva and Agastya in the Latter Part of the great Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa.

3.17.s:
daṇḍanāthāviniryāṇe saṃkhyātītaiḥ sitaprabhaiḥ /
chatrairgaganamāreje niḥsaṃkhyāśaśimaṇḍitam //
3.17.d:
दण्डनाथाविनिर्याणे संख्यातीतैः सितप्रभैः ।
छत्रैर्गगनमारेजे निःसंख्याशशिमण्डितम् ॥
3.17.m: Upon Daṇḍanāthā's departure, the sky shone with countless bright white umbrellas / as though filled with innumerable discs of the moon.

3.17.s:
anyonyasaktairthavalacchatrairantarghanībhavat /
timiraṃ nunude bhūyastatkāṇḍamaṇirociṣā //
3.17.d:
अन्योन्यसक्तैर्थवलच्छत्रैरन्तर्घनीभवत् ।
तिमिरं नुनुदे भूयस्तत्काण्डमणिरोचिषा ॥
3.17.m: The darkness growing dense within the cluster of white umbrellas closely joined together / was dispelled once more by the radiance of the jewels on their shafts.

3.17.s:
vajraprabhādhagadhagacchāyāpūritadiṅmukhāḥ /
tālavṛntāḥ śatavidhāḥ kroḍamukhyā bale 'calan //
3.17.d:
वज्रप्रभाधगधगच्छायापूरितदिङ्मुखाः ।
तालवृन्ताः शतविधाः क्रोडमुख्या बले ऽचलन् ॥
3.17.m: With fan-palms of a hundred kinds filling the directions with shadows glittering like lightning, / the boar-faced goddess advanced amidst her army.

3.17.s:
caṇḍo daṇḍādayastīvrābhairavāḥ śulapāṇayaḥ /
jvalatkeśāpiśaṅgābhāstaḍidbhāsuradiṅmukhāḥ //
3.17.d:
चण्डो दण्डादयस्तीव्राभैरवाः शुलपाणयः ।
ज्वलत्केशापिशङ्गाभास्तडिद्भासुरदिङ्मुखाः ॥
3.17.m: The fierce Bhairavas, such as Caṇḍa, Daṇḍa, and others, armed with tridents, / having blazing hair of reddish-yellow hue, illuminating the quarters like lightning,

3.17.s:
dahatya iva daityaughāṃstīkṣṇairmārgaṇavahnibhiḥ /
pracelurdaṇḍanāthāyāssenā nāsīradhāvitāḥ //
3.17.d:
दहत्य इव दैत्यौघांस्तीक्ष्णैर्मार्गणवह्निभिः ।
प्रचेलुर्दण्डनाथायास्सेना नासीरधाविताः ॥
3.17.m: As if consuming the hosts of Daityas with the sharp fires of their arrows, / marched forward, rushing to the front of Daṇḍanāthā's army.

3.17.s:
atha potrīmukhīdevīsamānākṛtibhūṣaṇāḥ /
tatsamānāyudhakarāstatsamānasvavāhanāḥ //
3.17.d:
अथ पोत्रीमुखीदेवीसमानाकृतिभूषणाः ।
तत्समानायुधकरास्तत्समानस्ववाहनाः ॥
3.17.m: Then [goddesses] having forms and ornaments identical to Goddess Potrīmukhī, / with identical weapons in their hands and identical mounts of their own,

3.17.s:
tīkṣmadaṃṣṭa3viniṣṭhyūtavahridhūmāmitāṃbarāḥ /
tamālaśyāmalākārāḥ kapilāḥ krūralocanāḥ //
3.17.d:
तीक्ष्मदंष्ट3विनिष्ठ्यूतवह्रिधूमामितांबराः ।
तमालश्यामलाकाराः कपिलाः क्रूरलोचनाः ॥
3.17.m: Spitting out from their sharp tusks smoke and fire that filled the sky, / dark in appearance like tamāla trees, tawny-haired, with cruel eyes,

3.17.s:
sahasramahiṣārūḍhāḥ praceluḥ sūkarānanāḥ /
atha śrīdaṇḍanāthā ca karicakrarathottamāt //
3.17.d:
सहस्रमहिषारूढाः प्रचेलुः सूकराननाः ।
अथ श्रीदण्डनाथा च करिचक्ररथोत्तमात् ॥
3.17.m: Boar-faced, mounted upon thousands of buffaloes, marched forward. / Then the venerable Daṇḍanāthā, from the supreme chariot Karicakra,

3.17.s:
avaruhya mahāsiṃhamāruroha svavāhanam /
vajraghoṣa iti khyātaṃ dhūtakesaramaṇḍalam //
3.17.d:
अवरुह्य महासिंहमारुरोह स्ववाहनम् ।
वज्रघोष इति ख्यातं धूतकेसरमण्डलम् ॥
3.17.m: Descended and mounted her own vehicle, a great lion / known as Vajraghoṣa, whose mane shook,

3.17.s:
vyaktāsyaṃ vikaṭākāraṃ viśaṅkaṭavilocanam /
daṃṣṭrākaṭakaṭatkārabadhirīkṛtadiktaṭam //
3.17.d:
व्यक्तास्यं विकटाकारं विशङ्कटविलोचनम् ।
दंष्ट्राकटकटत्कारबधिरीकृतदिक्तटम् ॥
3.17.m: With open mouth, formidable shape, and wide eyes, / deafening the regions of the quarters with the gnashing of its fangs,

3.17.s:
ādikūrmakaṭhorāsthi kharparapratimairnakhaiḥ /
vibantamiva bhūcakramāpātālaṃ nimajjibhiḥ //
3.17.d:
आदिकूर्मकठोरास्थि खर्परप्रतिमैर्नखैः ।
विबन्तमिव भूचक्रमापातालं निमज्जिभिः ॥
3.17.m: With claws resembling the shell-pieces of the hard bone of the Primeval Tortoise, / tearing the orb of the earth as they plunged down to Pātāla,

3.17.s:
yojanatrayamuttuṅgaṃ vagāduddhūtavāladhim /
siṃhavāhanamāruhya vyacaladdaṇḍanāyikā //
3.17.d:
योजनत्रयमुत्तुङ्गं वगादुद्धूतवालधिम् ।
सिंहवाहनमारुह्य व्यचलद्दण्डनायिका ॥
3.17.m: Three yojanas tall, its tail raised and swinging; / mounting this lion vehicle, Daṇḍanāyikā advanced.

3.17.s:
tasyāmasurasaṃhāre pravṛttāyāṃ jvalatkrudhi /
udvegaṃ bahulaṃ prāpa trailokyaṃ sacarācaram //
3.17.d:
तस्यामसुरसंहारे प्रवृत्तायां ज्वलत्क्रुधि ।
उद्वेगं बहुलं प्राप त्रैलोक्यं सचराचरम् ॥
3.17.m: As she set out to destroy the Asuras, her anger blazing, / the three worlds, both moving and unmoving, were seized with great agitation.

3.17.s:
kimasau dhakṣyati ruṣā viśvamadyaiva potriṇī /
kiṃ vā musalaghātena bhūmiṃ dvedhā kariṣyati //
3.17.d:
किमसौ धक्ष्यति रुषा विश्वमद्यैव पोत्रिणी ।
किं वा मुसलघातेन भूमिं द्वेधा करिष्यति ॥
3.17.m: “Will this boar-faced goddess consume the universe in her fury this very day? / Or will she cleave the earth in two with a blow of her pestle?

3.17.s:
atha vā halanirghātaiḥ kṣobhayiṣyati vāridhīn /
iti trastahṛdaḥ sarve gagane nākināṃ gaṇāḥ //
3.17.d:
अथ वा हलनिर्घातैः क्षोभयिष्यति वारिधीन् ।
इति त्रस्तहृदः सर्वे गगने नाकिनां गणाः ॥
3.17.m: Or will she agitate the oceans with the impacts of her plough?” / Thus terrified in heart, all the hosts of gods in the sky

3.17.s:
dūrādrutaṃ vimānaiśca satrāsaṃ dadṛśurgatāḥ /
vavandire ca tā devā baddhāñjalipuṭānvitāḥ /
muhurdvādaśanāmāni kīrtayanto nabhastale //
3.17.d:
दूराद्रुतं विमानैश्च सत्रासं ददृशुर्गताः ।
ववन्दिरे च ता देवा बद्धाञ्जलिपुटान्विताः ।
मुहुर्द्वादशनामानि कीर्तयन्तो नभस्तले ॥
3.17.m: Went in their aerial chariots and watched from afar in haste and fear; / and the gods bowed with hands folded in supplication, / repeatedly praising her twelve names in the vault of heaven.

3.17.s:
agastya uvāca
kāni dvādaśanāmāni tasyā devyā vada prabho /
aśvānana mahāprājña yeṣu me kautukaṃ mahat //
3.17.d:
अगस्त्य उवाच
कानि द्वादशनामानि तस्या देव्या वद प्रभो ।
अश्वानन महाप्राज्ञ येषु मे कौतुकं महत् ॥
3.17.m: Agastya said: / Tell me, O Lord, what are the twelve names of that goddess? / O horse-faced one of great wisdom, in which I have great curiosity!

3.17.s:
hayagrīva uvāca
śṛṇu dvādaśanāmāni tasyā devyā ghaṭodbhava /
yadākarṇanamātreṇa prasannā sā bhaviṣyati /
pañcamī daṇḍanāthā ca saṃketā samayeśvarī //
3.17.d:
हयग्रीव उवाच
शृणु द्वादशनामानि तस्या देव्या घटोद्भव ।
यदाकर्णनमात्रेण प्रसन्ना सा भविष्यति ।
पञ्चमी दण्डनाथा च संकेता समयेश्वरी ॥
3.17.m: Hayagrīva said: / Hear the twelve names of that goddess, O pot-born one, / merely by hearing which she becomes pleased: / Pañcamī, Daṇḍanāthā, Saṃketā, Samayeśvarī,

3.17.s:
tathā samayasaṃketā vārāhī potriṇī tathā /
vārtālī ca mahāsenāpyājñā cakreśvarī tathā //
3.17.d:
तथा समयसंकेता वाराही पोत्रिणी तथा ।
वार्ताली च महासेनाप्याज्ञा चक्रेश्वरी तथा ॥
3.17.m: likewise Samayasaṃketā, Vārāhī, and Potriṇī, / Vārtālī, Mahāsenā, Ājñā, Cakreśvarī,

3.17.s:
arighnī ceti samproktaṃ nāmadvādaśakaṃ mune /
nāmadvādaśakābhikhyavajrapañjaramadhyagaḥ /
saṃkaṭe duḥkhamāpnoti na kadācana mānavaḥ //
3.17.d:
अरिघ्नी चेति सम्प्रोक्तं नामद्वादशकं मुने ।
नामद्वादशकाभिख्यवज्रपञ्जरमध्यगः ।
संकटे दुःखमाप्नोति न कदाचन मानवः ॥
3.17.m: and Arighnī: thus the twelve names have been declared, O sage. / Standing within the adamantine cage known as the twelve names, / a man never meets with suffering in calamity.

3.17.s:
etairnāmabhirabhrasthāḥ saṃketāṃ bahu tuṣṭuvuḥ /
teṣāmanugrahārthāya pracacālaca sā punaḥ //
3.17.d:
एतैर्नामभिरभ्रस्थाः संकेतां बहु तुष्टुवुः ।
तेषामनुग्रहार्थाय प्रचचालच सा पुनः ॥
3.17.m: Standing in the sky, they praised Saṃketā abundantly with these names; / and for the sake of granting them grace, she set out again.

3.17.s:
atha saṃketayoginyā mantranāthā padaspṛśaḥ /
niryāṇasūcanakarī divi dadhvāna kāhalī //
3.17.d:
अथ संकेतयोगिन्या मन्त्रनाथा पदस्पृशः ।
निर्याणसूचनकरी दिवि दध्वान काहली ॥
3.17.m: Then the horn indicating departure sounded in heaven / for Mantranāthā, who touches the feet of the Saṃketayoginī.

3.17.s:
śṛṅgāraprāyabhūṣāṇāṃ śārdūlaśyāmalatviṣām /
vīṇāsaṃyatapāṇīnāṃ śaktīnāṃ niryayau balam //
3.17.d:
शृङ्गारप्रायभूषाणां शार्दूलश्यामलत्विषाम् ।
वीणासंयतपाणीनां शक्तीनां निर्ययौ बलम् ॥
3.17.m: The army of śaktis went forth, / adorned mostly with erotic ornaments, / lustrous with the dark hue of tigers, their hands holding vīṇās.

3.17.s:
kāścadgāyanti nṛtyanti mattakokilaniḥsvanāḥ /
vīṇāveṇumṛdaṅgādyāḥ savilāsapadakramāḥ //
3.17.d:
काश्चद्गायन्ति नृत्यन्ति मत्तकोकिलनिःस्वनाः ।
वीणावेणुमृदङ्गाद्याः सविलासपदक्रमाः ॥
3.17.m: Some were singing, some dancing, their voices like intoxicated cuckoos, / with vīṇās, flutes, mṛdaṅgas, and other instruments, their footsteps graceful.

3.17.s:
praceluḥ śaktayaḥ śyāmā harṣayantyo jagajjanān /
mayūravāhanāḥ kāścitkaticiddhaṃsavāhanāḥ //
3.17.d:
प्रचेलुः शक्तयः श्यामा हर्षयन्त्यो जगज्जनान् ।
मयूरवाहनाः काश्चित्कतिचिद्धंसवाहनाः ॥
3.17.m: The dark śaktis marched forth, delighting the folk of the world; / some rode peacocks, some rode swans,

3.17.s:
katicinnakulārūḍhāḥ katicitkokilāsanāḥ /
sarvāśca śyāmalākārāḥ kāścitkarṇīrathasthitāḥ //
3.17.d:
कतिचिन्नकुलारूढाः कतिचित्कोकिलासनाः ।
सर्वाश्च श्यामलाकाराः काश्चित्कर्णीरथस्थिताः ॥
3.17.m: some were mounted on mongooses, some seated on cuckoos; / all were dark of form, and some stood upon sedan chairs.

3.17.s:
kādaṃbamadhumattāśca kāścidārūḍhasaindhavāḥ /
mantranāthāṃ puraskṛtya saṃpraceluḥ puraḥ puraḥ //
3.17.d:
कादंबमधुमत्ताश्च काश्चिदारूढसैन्धवाः ।
मन्त्रनाथां पुरस्कृत्य संप्रचेलुः पुरः पुरः ॥
3.17.m: Intoxicated with kadaṃba honey, and some mounted on horses, / they advanced ahead and ahead, placing Mantranāthā at their head.

3.17.s:
athāruhya samuttuṅgadhvajacakraṃ mahāratham /
bālārkavarṇakavacā madālolavilocanā //
3.17.d:
अथारुह्य समुत्तुङ्गध्वजचक्रं महारथम् ।
बालार्कवर्णकवचा मदालोलविलोचना ॥
3.17.m: Then, having mounted the great chariot whose flagstaff-cakra rose high, / clad in armor the color of the rising sun, her eyes fluttering with intoxication,

3.17.s:
īṣatprasvedakaṇikāmanoharamukhāṃbujā /
prekṣayantī kaṭākṣaudhauḥ kiñcidbhrūvallitāṇḍavaiḥ //
3.17.d:
ईषत्प्रस्वेदकणिकामनोहरमुखांबुजा ।
प्रेक्षयन्ती कटाक्षौधौः किञ्चिद्भ्रूवल्लिताण्डवैः ॥
3.17.m: her lotus face charming with tiny drops of sweat, / gazing with streams of side-glances through slight dances of her creeper-like brows,

3.17.s:
samastamapi tatsainyaṃ śaktīnāmuddhatoddhatam /
picchatrikoṇacchatreṇa birudena mahīyasā //
3.17.d:
समस्तमपि तत्सैन्यं शक्तीनामुद्धतोद्धतम् ।
पिच्छत्रिकोणच्छत्रेण बिरुदेन महीयसा ॥
3.17.m: at the entire fierce and haughty army of śaktis, / accompanied by a peacock-feather triangular umbrella, a glorious emblem of honor,

3.17.s:
āsāṃ madhye na cānyāsāṃ śaktīnāmujjvalodayā /
nirjagāma ghanaśyāmaśyāmalā mantranāyikā //
3.17.d:
आसां मध्ये न चान्यासां शक्तीनामुज्ज्वलोदया ।
निर्जगाम घनश्यामश्यामला मन्त्रनायिका ॥
3.17.m: in the midst of these—and no other—śaktis, radiant in her rising, / Mantranāyikā went forth, dark as a rain-cloud.

3.17.s:
tāṃ tuṣṭuvuḥ ṣoḍaśabhirnāmabhirnākavāsinaḥ /
tāni ṣoḍaśanāmāni śṛṇu kuṃbhasamudbhava //
3.17.d:
तां तुष्टुवुः षोडशभिर्नामभिर्नाकवासिनः ।
तानि षोडशनामानि शृणु कुंभसमुद्भव ॥
3.17.m: The dwellers of heaven praised her with sixteen names. / Hear those sixteen names, O pot-born one:

3.17.s:
saṃgītayoginī śyāmā śyāmalā mantranāyikā /
mantriṇī saciveśī ca pradhāneśī śukapriyā //
3.17.d:
संगीतयोगिनी श्यामा श्यामला मन्त्रनायिका ।
मन्त्रिणी सचिवेशी च प्रधानेशी शुकप्रिया ॥
3.17.m: Saṃgītayoginī, Śyāmā, Śyāmalā, Mantranāyikā, / Mantriṇī, Saciveśī, Pradhāneśī, Śukapriyā,

3.17.s:
vīṇāvatī vaiṇikī ca mudriṇī priyakapriyā /
nipapriyā kadaṃbeśī kadaṃbavanavāsinī //
3.17.d:
वीणावती वैणिकी च मुद्रिणी प्रियकप्रिया ।
निपप्रिया कदंबेशी कदंबवनवासिनी ॥
3.17.m: Vīṇāvatī, Vaiṇikī, Mudriṇī, Priyakapriyā, / Nipapriyā, Kadaṃbeśī, Kadaṃbavanavāsinī,

3.17.s:
sadāmadā ca nāmāni ṣoḍaśaitāni kuṃbhaja /
etairyaḥ saciveśānīṃ sakṛtstauti śarīravān /
tasya trailokyamakhilaṃ haste tiṣṭhatyasaṃśayam //
3.17.d:
सदामदा च नामानि षोडशैतानि कुंभज ।
एतैर्यः सचिवेशानीं सकृत्स्तौति शरीरवान् ।
तस्य त्रैलोक्यमखिलं हस्ते तिष्ठत्यसंशयम् ॥
3.17.m: and Sadāmadā: these are the sixteen names, O pot-born one. / Whosoever among embodied beings praises Saciveśānī once with these, / the entire threefold world rests in his hand, without doubt.

3.17.s:
mantrināthā yatrayatra kaṭākṣaṃ vikiratyasau /
tatratatra gatāśaṅkaṃ śatrusainyaṃ patatyalam //
3.17.d:
मन्त्रिनाथा यत्रयत्र कटाक्षं विकिरत्यसौ ।
तत्रतत्र गताशङ्कं शत्रुसैन्यं पतत्यलम् ॥
3.17.m: Wherever Mantrināthā casts her side-glance, / there the enemy army falls abundantly, all apprehension gone.

3.17.s:
lalitāparameśānyā rājyacarcā tu yāvatī /
śaktīnāmapi carcā yā sā sarvatra jayapradā //
3.17.d:
ललितापरमेशान्या राज्यचर्चा तु यावती ।
शक्तीनामपि चर्चा या सा सर्वत्र जयप्रदा ॥
3.17.m: Whatever governance Lalitā, the Supreme Sovereign, possesses, / and whatever governance the śaktis possess, it grants victory everywhere.

3.17.s:
atha saṃgītayoginyāḥ karasthācchukapotakāt /
nirjagāma dhanurvedo vahansajjaṃśarāsanam //
3.17.d:
अथ संगीतयोगिन्याः करस्थाच्छुकपोतकात् ।
निर्जगाम धनुर्वेदो वहन्सज्जंशरासनम् ॥
3.17.m: Then, from the young parrot perched upon the hand of the Saṃgītayoginī, / Dhanurveda emerged, bearing a strung bow.

3.17.s:
caturbāhuyuto vīrastriśirāstrivilocanaḥ /
namaskṛtya pradhāneśīmidamāha sa bhaktimān //
3.17.d:
चतुर्बाहुयुतो वीरस्त्रिशिरास्त्रिविलोचनः ।
नमस्कृत्य प्रधानेशीमिदमाह स भक्तिमान् ॥
3.17.m: Possessed of four arms, heroic, three-headed, and three-eyed, / having bowed down to Pradhāneśī, the devout one spoke this:

3.17.s:
devi bhaṇḍāsuredrasya yuddhāya tvaṃ pravarttase /
atastava mayā sāhyaṃ kartavyaṃ mantrināyike //
3.17.d:
देवि भण्डासुरेद्रस्य युद्धाय त्वं प्रवर्त्तसे ।
अतस्तव मया साह्यं कर्तव्यं मन्त्रिनायिके ॥
3.17.m: "O goddess, you are setting forth to do battle with the demon-king Bhaṇḍa; / therefore, assistance must be rendered by me, O Mantrināyikā.

3.17.s:
catrajīvamimaṃ nāma kodaṇḍaṃ sumahattaram /
gṛhāṇa jagatāmaṃba dānavānāṃ nibarhaṇam //
3.17.d:
चत्रजीवमिमं नाम कोदण्डं सुमहत्तरम् ।
गृहाण जगतामंब दानवानां निबर्हणम् ॥
3.17.m: Take this exceedingly great bow named Citrajīva, / O Mother of the worlds, which destroys the dānavas!

3.17.s:
imau cākṣayabāṇāḍhyau tūṇīrau svarṇacitritau /
gṛhāṇa daityanāśāya mamānugrahahetave //
3.17.d:
इमौ चाक्षयबाणाढ्यौ तूणीरौ स्वर्णचित्रितौ ।
गृहाण दैत्यनाशाय ममानुग्रहहेतवे ॥
3.17.m: And take these two quivers decorated with gold, filled with inexhaustible arrows, / for the destruction of the daityas and for the sake of blessing me!"

3.17.s:
iti praṇamya śirasā dhanurvedena bhaktitaḥ /
arpitāṃścāpatūṇīrāñjagrāha priyakapriyā //
3.17.d:
इति प्रणम्य शिरसा धनुर्वेदेन भक्तितः ।
अर्पितांश्चापतूणीराञ्जग्राह प्रियकप्रिया ॥
3.17.m: Thus bowing with his head in devotion, / Priyakapriyā accepted the bow and quivers offered by Dhanurveda.

3.17.s:
citrajīvaṃ mahācāpamādāya ca śūkapriyā /
visphāraṃ janayāmāsa maurvīmudvādya bhūriśaḥ //
3.17.d:
चित्रजीवं महाचापमादाय च शूकप्रिया ।
विस्फारं जनयामास मौर्वीमुद्वाद्य भूरिशः ॥
3.17.m: Taking the great bow Citrajīva, Śukapriyā / produced a loud twang, repeatedly plucking the bowstring.

3.17.s:
saṃgītayoginī cāpadhvaninā pūritaṃ jagat /
nākālayānāṃ ca manona yanānandasaṃpadā //
3.17.d:
संगीतयोगिनी चापध्वनिना पूरितं जगत् ।
नाकालयानां च मनोन यनानन्दसंपदा ॥
3.17.m: The world was filled with the sound of the bow of the Saṃgītayoginī, / and the minds of the dwellers of heaven were filled with a wealth of visual delight.

3.17.s:
yantriṇī ceti dve tasyāḥ paricārike /
śukaṃ vīṇāṃ ca sahasā vahantyau pariceratuḥ //
3.17.d:
यन्त्रिणी चेति द्वे तस्याः परिचारिके ।
शुकं वीणां च सहसा वहन्त्यौ परिचेरतुः ॥
3.17.m: […] and Yantriṇī, her two attendants, / quickly attended upon her, carrying the parrot and the vīṇā.

3.17.s:
ālolavalayakvāṇavardhiṣṇuguṇanisvanam /
dhārayantī ghanaśyāmā cakārātimanoharam //
3.17.d:
आलोलवलयक्वाणवर्धिष्णुगुणनिस्वनम् ।
धारयन्ती घनश्यामा चकारातिमनोहरम् ॥
3.17.m: Holding [the bow], she who is dark as a rain-cloud made [it] exceedingly captivating, / the twang of the string swelling with the jingling of her tremulous bracelets.

3.17.s:
citrajīvaśarāsena bhūṣitā gītayoginī /
kadaṃbinīva ruruce kadambacchatrakārmukā //
3.17.d:
चित्रजीवशरासेन भूषिता गीतयोगिनी ।
कदंबिनीव रुरुचे कदम्बच्छत्रकार्मुका ॥
3.17.m: Adorned with the Citrajīva bow, Gītayoginī / shone like a bank of clouds with an umbrella and bow of kadamba [blossoms].

3.17.s:
kālīkaṭākṣavattīkṣṇo nṛtyadbhujagabhīṣaṇaḥ /
ullasandakṣiṇe pāṇau vilalāsa śilīmukhaḥ //
3.17.d:
कालीकटाक्षवत्तीक्ष्णो नृत्यद्भुजगभीषणः ।
उल्लसन्दक्षिणे पाणौ विललास शिलीमुखः ॥
3.17.m: Sharp as the side-glance of Kālī, terrifying as a dancing serpent, / an arrow glittered, shining in her right hand.

3.17.s:
geyacakrarathārūḍhāṃ tāṃ paścācca siṣevire /
tadvacchyāmalaśobhāḍhyā devyo bāṇadhanurdharāḥ //
3.17.d:
गेयचक्ररथारूढां तां पश्चाच्च सिषेविरे ।
तद्वच्छ्यामलशोभाढ्या देव्यो बाणधनुर्धराः ॥
3.17.m: And behind her, mounted on the Geyacakra chariot, / goddesses endowed with dark splendor, bearing bows and arrows, attended upon her—

3.17.s:
sahasrākṣauhiṇīsaṃkhyāstīvravegā madālasāḥ /
āpūrayantyaḥ kakubhaṃ kalaiḥ kilikilāravaiḥ //
iti śrībrahmāṇḍamahāpurāṇe uttarabhāge hayagrīvāgastyasaṃvāde lalitopākhyāne daṇḍanāthāśyāmalāsenāyātrā nāma saptadaśo 'dhyāyaḥ
3.17.d:
सहस्राक्षौहिणीसंख्यास्तीव्रवेगा मदालसाः ।
आपूरयन्त्यः ककुभं कलैः किलिकिलारवैः ॥
इति श्रीब्रह्माण्डमहापुराणे उत्तरभागे हयग्रीवागस्त्यसंवादे ललितोपाख्याने दण्डनाथाश्यामलासेनायात्रा नाम सप्तदशो ऽध्यायः
3.17.m:
a thousand akṣauhiṇīs in number, of fierce speed, languid with intoxication, / filling the quarters of the sky with melodious shouts of joy.

Thus ends the seventeenth chapter, named 'The March of the Armies of Daṇḍanāthā and Śyāmalā', in the Lalitopākhyāna, in the dialogue between Hayagrīva and Agastya, in the latter section of the glorious Brahmāṇḍamahāpurāṇa.

3.18.s:
atha rājanāyikā śritājvalitāṅkuśā phaṇisamānapāśabhṛt /
kalanikvaṇadvalayamaikṣvaṃ dhanurdadhatī pradīptakusumeṣupañcakā //
3.18.d:
अथ राजनायिका श्रिताज्वलिताङ्कुशा फणिसमानपाशभृत् ।
कलनिक्वणद्वलयमैक्ष्वं धनुर्दधती प्रदीप्तकुसुमेषुपञ्चका ॥
3.18.m: Then Rājanāyikā, holding a blazing goad, holding a noose resembling a serpent, / bearing a sugarcane bow with gently tinkling bracelets, and holding the five flaming flower-arrows,

3.18.s:
udayatsahatsramahasā sahasrato 'pyatipāṭalaṃ nijavapuḥ prabhājharam /
kiratī diśāsu vadanasya kāntibhiḥ sṛjatīva candramayamabhramaṇḍalam //
3.18.d:
उदयत्सहत्स्रमहसा सहस्रतो ऽप्यतिपाटलं निजवपुः प्रभाझरम् ।
किरती दिशासु वदनस्य कान्तिभिः सृजतीव चन्द्रमयमभ्रमण्डलम् ॥
3.18.m: scattering into the directions a stream of radiance from her own body, far redder than a thousand rising suns, / as if creating a sky-orb composed of moons by the splendors of her face,

3.18.s:
daśayojanāyatimātā jagattrayīmabhivṛṇvatā viśadamauktikātmanā /
dhavalātapatravalayena bhāsurā śaśimaṇḍalasya sakhitāmupeyuṣā //
3.18.d:
दशयोजनायतिमाता जगत्त्रयीमभिवृण्वता विशदमौक्तिकात्मना ।
धवलातपत्रवलयेन भासुरा शशिमण्डलस्य सखितामुपेयुषा ॥
3.18.m: shining with a circle of a white parasol, ten yojanas in extent, / covering the three worlds, made of pure pearls, attaining friendship with the disc of the moon,

3.18.s:
abhivījitā ca maṇikāntaśobhinā vijayādimukhyaparicārikāgaṇaiḥ /
navacandrikālaharikāntikandalīcatureṇa cāmaracatuṣṭayena ca //
3.18.d:
अभिवीजिता च मणिकान्तशोभिना विजयादिमुख्यपरिचारिकागणैः ।
नवचन्द्रिकालहरिकान्तिकन्दलीचतुरेण चामरचतुष्टयेन च ॥
3.18.m: fanned by the host of principal attendants beginning with Vijayā, radiant with lovely gems, / and by four chowries skilled at sprouting sprays of brilliance like waves of fresh moonlight,

manifesting the status of sole sovereignty over the śaktis, her army-realm adorned with hundreds of signs of imperial rule, / her majesty praised by immortal women with arrangements of music and instruments, her splendor clear,
beyond the range of words, beyond the very range of intellect, not to be conceived in such a manner, peerless,

touching the pride of the imperial wealth of the cakra of śaktis that filled the interior of the three worlds, / served from near at hand by those competing to be first, who bound high añjalis of devotion upon their heads,

3.18.s:
brahmeśaviṣṇuvṛṣamukhyasurottamānāṃ vaktrāṇivarṣitanutīni kaṭākṣayantī /
uddīptapuṣpaśarapañcakataḥ samutthaijyotirmayaṃ tribhuvanaṃ sahasā dadhānā //
3.18.d:
ब्रह्मेशविष्णुवृषमुख्यसुरोत्तमानां वक्त्राणिवर्षितनुतीनि कटाक्षयन्ती ।
उद्दीप्तपुष्पशरपञ्चकतः समुत्थैज्योतिर्मयं त्रिभुवनं सहसा दधाना ॥
3.18.m: side-glancing at the faces showering praise of the foremost gods headed by Brahmā, Īśa, Viṣṇu, and the Bull[-bannered Śiva], / suddenly holding the three worlds filled with light arising from her five blazing flower-arrows—

Shower of auspicious parched grain tossed by crowds of Apsarases with lightning-like luster, / with Kāmeśvarī and the others of lovely radiance, exceedingly enchanting in their array of battle-attire,

attended close to her feet by the Nityās whose weapons' luster eclipsed the sun, / while high aloft, the crowning emblem named the Śrīcakra, having a pennant ten yojanas high, brushed the mass of clouds,

3.18.s:
tīvrābhirāvaṇasuśaktiparaṃparabhiryuktaṃ rathaṃ samarakarmaṇi cālayantī /
prodyatpiśaṅgarucibhāgamalāṃśukena vītāmanohararucissamare vyabhāsīt //
3.18.d:
तीव्राभिरावणसुशक्तिपरंपरभिर्युक्तं रथं समरकर्मणि चालयन्ती ।
प्रोद्यत्पिशङ्गरुचिभागमलांशुकेन वीतामनोहररुचिस्समरे व्यभासीत् ॥
3.18.m: driving in the work of battle her chariot equipped with succession after succession of fierce, splendid Śaktis, / clad in a garment of flawless cloth possessing a rising reddish-yellow glow, she shone with enchanting radiance in battle.

3.18.s:
pañcādhikairviśatināmaratnaiḥ prapañcapāpapraśamātidakṣaiḥ /
saṃstūyamānā lalitā marudbhiḥ saṃgrāmamuddiśya samuccacāla //
3.18.d:
पञ्चाधिकैर्विशतिनामरत्नैः प्रपञ्चपापप्रशमातिदक्षैः ।
संस्तूयमाना ललिता मरुद्भिः संग्राममुद्दिश्य समुच्चचाल ॥
3.18.m: Praised by the Maruts with twenty-five gem-like names / most capable of quelling the sins of worldly manifestation, Lalitā set forth toward the battle.

3.18.s:
agastya uvāca
vījivaktra mahābuddhe pañcaviṃśatināmabhiḥ /
lalitāparameśānyā dehi karṇarasāyanam //
3.18.d:
अगस्त्य उवाच
वीजिवक्त्र महाबुद्धे पञ्चविंशतिनामभिः ।
ललितापरमेशान्या देहि कर्णरसायनम् ॥
3.18.m: Agastya said: / O horse-faced one of vast intellect, grant as an elixir to the ears / the twenty-five names of the supreme sovereign Lalitā!

3.18.s:
hayagrīva uvāca
siṃhāsanā śrīlalitā mahārājñī parāṅkuśā /
cāpinī tripurā caiva mahātripurasundarī //
3.18.d:
हयग्रीव उवाच
सिंहासना श्रीललिता महाराज्ञी पराङ्कुशा ।
चापिनी त्रिपुरा चैव महात्रिपुरसुन्दरी ॥
3.18.m: Hayagrīva said: / Siṃhāsanā, Śrīlalitā, Mahārājñī, Parāṅkuśā, / Cāpinī, Tripurā, and Mahātripurasundarī,

3.18.s:
sundarī cakranāthā ca sāmrājī cakriṇī tathā /
cakreśvarī mahādevī kāmeśī parameśvarī //
3.18.d:
सुन्दरी चक्रनाथा च साम्राजी चक्रिणी तथा ।
चक्रेश्वरी महादेवी कामेशी परमेश्वरी ॥
3.18.m: Sundarī, Cakranāthā, Sāmrājñī, and Cakriṇī, / Cakreśvarī, Mahādevī, Kāmeśī, Parameśvarī,

3.18.s:
kāmarājapriyā kāmakoṭigā cakravartinī /
mahāvidyā śivānaṅgavallabhā sarvapāṭalā //
3.18.d:
कामराजप्रिया कामकोटिगा चक्रवर्तिनी ।
महाविद्या शिवानङ्गवल्लभा सर्वपाटला ॥
3.18.m: Kāmarājapriyā, Kāmakoṭigā, Cakravartinī, / Mahāvidyā, Śivā, Anaṅgavallabhā, Sarvapāṭalā,
Kulanāthā, Āmnāyanāthā, Sarvāmnāyanivāsinī, / and Śṛṅgāranāyikā—with these twenty-five names,

3.18.s:
stuvanti ye mahābhāgāṃ lalitāṃ parameśvarīm /
te prāpnuvanti saubhāgyamaṣṭau siddhīrmahadyaśaḥ //
3.18.d:
स्तुवन्ति ये महाभागां ललितां परमेश्वरीम् ।
ते प्राप्नुवन्ति सौभाग्यमष्टौ सिद्धीर्महद्यशः ॥
3.18.m: those who praise the illustrious supreme sovereign Lalitā / attain good fortune, the eight supernatural powers, and great renown.

3.18.s:
itthaṃ pracaṇḍasaṃraṃbhaṃ cālayantī mahadbalam /
bhaṇḍāsuraṃ prati kruddhā cacāla lalitāṃbikā //
iti śrībrahmāṇḍamahāpurāṇe uttarabhāge hayagrīvāgastyasaṃvāde lalitopākhyāne lalitāparameśvarīsenājaya yātrā nāmāṣṭādaśo 'dhyāyaḥ
3.18.d:
इत्थं प्रचण्डसंरंभं चालयन्ती महद्बलम् ।
भण्डासुरं प्रति क्रुद्धा चचाल ललितांबिका ॥
इति श्रीब्रह्माण्डमहापुराणे उत्तरभागे हयग्रीवागस्त्यसंवादे ललितोपाख्याने ललितापरमेश्वरीसेनाजय यात्रा नामाष्टादशो ऽध्यायः
3.18.m:
Thus mobilizing that great force with fierce impetuosity, / Mother Lalitā, enraged against the demon Bhaṇḍa, marched forth.

Thus ends the eighteenth chapter, named ‘The Victory March of the Supreme Sovereign Lalitā’s Army’, in the Lalitopākhyāna, in the dialogue between Hayagrīva and Agastya, in the latter section of the glorious Brahmāṇḍa Mahāpurāṇa.

3.19.s:
agastya uvāca
cakrarājarathendrasya yāḥparvaṇi samāśritāḥ /
devatā prakaṭābhikhyāstāsāmākhyāṃ nivedaya //
3.19.d:
अगस्त्य उवाच
चक्रराजरथेन्द्रस्य याःपर्वणि समाश्रिताः ।
देवता प्रकटाभिख्यास्तासामाख्यां निवेदय ॥
3.19.m: Agastya said: / The deities situated on the steps of the foremost chariot of the Cakrarāja, / known as the Prakaṭa deities—reveal their names,

3.19.s:
saṃkhyāśca tāsāmakhilā varṇabhedāṃśca śobhanān /
āyudhāni ca divyāni kathayasva hayānana //
3.19.d:
संख्याश्च तासामखिला वर्णभेदांश्च शोभनान् ।
आयुधानि च दिव्यानि कथयस्व हयानन ॥
3.19.m: and all their numbers, their splendid distinctions of color, / and their divine weapons; declare them, O horse-faced one!

3.19.s:
hayagrīva uvāca
navamaṃ parva dīptasya rathasya samupasthitāḥ /
taśa proktā siddhidevyastāsāṃ nāmāni macchṛṇu //
3.19.d:
हयग्रीव उवाच
नवमं पर्व दीप्तस्य रथस्य समुपस्थिताः ।
तश प्रोक्ता सिद्धिदेव्यस्तासां नामानि मच्छृणु ॥
3.19.m: Hayagrīva said: / Stationed on the ninth step of that blazing chariot / are ten goddesses of supernatural powers; hear their names from me:

3.19.s:
aṇimā mahimācaiva laghimā garimā tathā /
īśitā vaśitā caiva prāptiḥ siddhiśca saptamī //
3.19.d:
अणिमा महिमाचैव लघिमा गरिमा तथा ।
ईशिता वशिता चैव प्राप्तिः सिद्धिश्च सप्तमी ॥
3.19.m: Aṇimā, Mahimā, Laghimā, and Garimā, / Īśitā, Vaśitā, and Prāpti as the seventh siddhi,

3.19.s:
prākāmyamuktisiddhiśca sarvakāmābhidhāparā /
etādevyaścaturbāhvyo japākusumasaṃnibhāḥ //
3.19.d:
प्राकाम्यमुक्तिसिद्धिश्च सर्वकामाभिधापरा ।
एतादेव्यश्चतुर्बाह्व्यो जपाकुसुमसंनिभाः ॥
3.19.m: Prākāmya, Muktisiddhi, and the supreme one named Sarvakāmā. / These four-armed goddesses resemble hibiscus flowers;

3.19.s:
cintāmaṇikapālaṃ ca triśūlaṃ siddhikajjalam /
dadhānā dayayā pūrṇā yogibhiśca niṣevitāḥ //
3.19.d:
चिन्तामणिकपालं च त्रिशूलं सिद्धिकज्जलम् ।
दधाना दयया पूर्णा योगिभिश्च निषेविताः ॥
3.19.m: holding the wish-fulfilling jewel, a skull-bowl, a trident, and the collyrium of supernatural powers, / they are filled with compassion and attended upon by yogins.

3.19.s:
tatra pūrvārddhabhāge ca brahmādyā aṣṭa śaktayaḥ /
brāhmī māheśvarī caiva kaumārī vaiṣmavī tathā /
vārāhī caiva māṃhendrī cāmuṇḍā caiva saptamī //
3.19.d:
तत्र पूर्वार्द्धभागे च ब्रह्माद्या अष्ट शक्तयः ।
ब्राह्मी माहेश्वरी चैव कौमारी वैष्मवी तथा ।
वाराही चैव मांहेन्द्री चामुण्डा चैव सप्तमी ॥
3.19.m: And there, in the eastern half, are the eight Śaktis beginning with Brahmā: / Brāhmī, Māheśvarī, Kaumārī, Vaiṣṇavī, / Vārāhī, Māhendrī, and Cāmuṇḍā as the seventh,

3.19.s:
mahālakṣmīraṣṭamī ca dvibhujāḥ śoṇavigrahāḥ /
kapālamutpalaṃ caiva bibhrāṇā raktavāsasaḥ //
3.19.d:
महालक्ष्मीरष्टमी च द्विभुजाः शोणविग्रहाः ।
कपालमुत्पलं चैव बिभ्राणा रक्तवाससः ॥
3.19.m: and Mahālakṣmī as the eighth; two-armed, with red-hued bodies, / bearing a skull-bowl and a blue lotus, clad in red garments.

3.19.s:
atha vānya prakāreṇa keciddhyānaṃ pacakṣate /
brahmādisadṛśākārā brahmādisadṛśāyudhāḥ //
3.19.d:
अथ वान्य प्रकारेण केचिद्ध्यानं पचक्षते ।
ब्रह्मादिसदृशाकारा ब्रह्मादिसदृशायुधाः ॥
3.19.m: Or else, according to another manner, some declare their meditation: / having forms resembling Brahmā and the others, weapons resembling Brahmā and the others,

3.19.s:
brahmādīnāṃ paraṃ cihnaṃ dhārayantyaḥ prakīrtitāḥ /
tāsāmūrdhvasthānagatāṃ mudrā devyo mahattarāḥ //
3.19.d:
ब्रह्मादीनां परं चिह्नं धारयन्त्यः प्रकीर्तिताः ।
तासामूर्ध्वस्थानगतां मुद्रा देव्यो महत्तराः ॥
3.19.m: they are proclaimed as bearing the supreme emblems of Brahmā and the rest. / Located in the upper position above them are the exalted Mudrā goddesses:

3.19.s:
mudrāviracanāyuktairhastaiḥ kamalakāntibhiḥ /
dāḍimīpuṣpasaṅkāśāḥ pītāṃbaramanoharāḥ //
3.19.d:
मुद्राविरचनायुक्तैर्हस्तैः कमलकान्तिभिः ।
दाडिमीपुष्पसङ्काशाः पीतांबरमनोहराः ॥
3.19.m: with hands formed in the shapes of mudrās, possessing the beauty of lotuses, / resembling pomegranate blossoms, captivating in yellow garments,

3.19.s:
caturbhujā bhujadvandvadhṛtacarmakṛpāṇakāḥ /
madaraktavilolākṣyastāsāṃ nāmāni macchṛṇu //
3.19.d:
चतुर्भुजा भुजद्वन्द्वधृतचर्मकृपाणकाः ।
मदरक्तविलोलाक्ष्यस्तासां नामानि मच्छृणु ॥
3.19.m: four-armed, bearing shields and swords in a pair of arms, / with restless eyes reddened by intoxicating passion; hear their names from me:

3.19.s:
sarvasaṃkṣobhiṇī caiva sarvavidrāviṇī tathā /
sarvākarṣaṇakṛnmudrā tathā sarvavaśaṅkarī //
3.19.d:
सर्वसंक्षोभिणी चैव सर्वविद्राविणी तथा ।
सर्वाकर्षणकृन्मुद्रा तथा सर्ववशङ्करी ॥
3.19.m: Sarvasaṃkṣobhiṇī, Sarvavidrāviṇī, / the mudrā Sarvākarṣaṇakṛt, and Sarvavaśaṅkarī,

3.19.s:
sarvonmādanamudrā ca yaṣṭiḥ sarvamahāṅkuśā /
sarvakhecarikā mudrā sarvabījā tathāparā //
3.19.d:
सर्वोन्मादनमुद्रा च यष्टिः सर्वमहाङ्कुशा ।
सर्वखेचरिका मुद्रा सर्वबीजा तथापरा ॥
3.19.m: Sarvonmādanamudrā, the staff Sarvamahāṅkuśā, / the mudrā Sarvakhecarī, another named Sarvabījā,

3.19.s:
sarvayoniśca navamī tathā sarvatriśaṇḍikā /
siddhibrāhayādimudrāstā etāḥ prakaṭaśaktayaḥ //
3.19.d:
सर्वयोनिश्च नवमी तथा सर्वत्रिशण्डिका ।
सिद्धिब्राहयादिमुद्रास्ता एताः प्रकटशक्तयः ॥
3.19.m: Sarvayoni as the ninth, and Sarvatrikhaṇḍikā. / These mudrās, together with the Siddhis, Brāhmī, and the rest, are the Prakaṭa Śaktis.

3.19.s:
bhaṇḍāsurasya saṃhāraṃ kartuṃ raktarathe sthitāḥ /
yā guptākhyāḥ pūrvamuktāstāsāṃ nāmāni macchṛṇu //
3.19.d:
भण्डासुरस्य संहारं कर्तुं रक्तरथे स्थिताः ।
या गुप्ताख्याः पूर्वमुक्तास्तासां नामानि मच्छृणु ॥
3.19.m: Stationed on the red chariot to bring about the destruction of the demon Bhaṇḍa, / those previously mentioned under the name Guptā—hear their names from me:

3.19.s:
kāmākarṣaṇikā caiva buddhyākarṣaṇikā kalā /
ahaṅkārākarṣiṇī ca śabdākarṣaṇikā kalā //
3.19.d:
कामाकर्षणिका चैव बुद्ध्याकर्षणिका कला ।
अहङ्काराकर्षिणी च शब्दाकर्षणिका कला ॥
3.19.m: Kāmākarṣaṇikā, the digit Buddhyākarṣaṇikā, / Ahaṅkārākarṣiṇī, and the digit Śabdākarṣaṇikā,

3.19.s:
sparśākarṣaṇikā nityā rūpākarṣaṇikā kalā /
rasākarṣaṇikā nityā gandhākarṣaṇikā kalā //
3.19.d:
स्पर्शाकर्षणिका नित्या रूपाकर्षणिका कला ।
रसाकर्षणिका नित्या गन्धाकर्षणिका कला ॥
3.19.m: the Nityā Sparśākarṣaṇikā, the digit Rūpākarṣaṇikā, / the Nityā Rasākarṣaṇikā, the digit Gandhākarṣaṇikā,

3.19.s:
cittākarṣaṇikā nityā dhairyākarṣaṇikā kalā /
smṛtyā karṣaṇikā nityā nāmākarṇaṇikā kalā //
3.19.d:
चित्ताकर्षणिका नित्या धैर्याकर्षणिका कला ।
स्मृत्या कर्षणिका नित्या नामाकर्णणिका कला ॥
3.19.m: the Nityā Cittākarṣaṇikā, the digit Dhairyākarṣaṇikā, / the Nityā Smṛtyākarṣaṇikā, the digit Nāmākarṣaṇikā,

3.19.s:
bījākarṣaṇikā nityā cātmakarṣaṇikā kalā /
amṛtākarṣaṇī nityā śarīrākarṣiṇī kalā //
3.19.d:
बीजाकर्षणिका नित्या चात्मकर्षणिका कला ।
अमृताकर्षणी नित्या शरीराकर्षिणी कला ॥
3.19.m: the Nityā Bījākarṣaṇikā, the digit Ātmākarṣaṇikā, / the Nityā Amṛtākarṣiṇī, and the digit Śarīrākarṣiṇī.

3.19.s:
etāḥ ṣoḍaśa śītāṃśukalārūpāśca śaktayaḥ /
aṣṭamaṃ parva samprāptā guptā nāmnā prakīrtitāḥ //
3.19.d:
एताः षोडश शीतांशुकलारूपाश्च शक्तयः ।
अष्टमं पर्व सम्प्राप्ता गुप्ता नाम्ना प्रकीर्तिताः ॥
3.19.m: These sixteen Śaktis embody the digits of the cool-rayed moon; / stationed on the eighth step, they are renowned by the name Guptā.

3.19.s:
vidrumadrumasaṅkāśā mandasmita manoharāḥ /
caturbhujāstrinetrāśca candrārkamukujojjvalāḥ //
3.19.d:
विद्रुमद्रुमसङ्काशा मन्दस्मित मनोहराः ।
चतुर्भुजास्त्रिनेत्राश्च चन्द्रार्कमुकुजोज्ज्वलाः ॥
3.19.m: Resembling coral trees, captivating with gentle smiles, / four-armed, three-eyed, radiant with crowns bearing the moon and sun,

3.19.s:
cāpabāṇau carmakhaḍgau dadhānā divyakāntayaḥ /
bhaṇḍāsuravadhārthāya pravṛttāḥ kumbhasambhava //
3.19.d:
चापबाणौ चर्मखड्गौ दधाना दिव्यकान्तयः ।
भण्डासुरवधार्थाय प्रवृत्ताः कुम्भसम्भव ॥
3.19.m: bearing bow, arrow, shield, and sword, of divine radiance, / they set forth for the slaying of the demon Bhaṇḍa, O pot-born one.

3.19.s:
sāyantanajvaladdīpaprakhyacakrarathasya tu /
saptame parvaṇi kṛtāvāsā guptatarābhidhāḥ //
3.19.d:
सायन्तनज्वलद्दीपप्रख्यचक्ररथस्य तु ।
सप्तमे पर्वणि कृतावासा गुप्ततराभिधाः ॥
3.19.m: Now, having made their abode on the seventh step / of the chariot-cakra that resembles a lamp burning in the evening, those named Guptatarā [stand]:

3.19.s:
anaṅgamadanānaṅgamadanāturayā saha /
anaṅgalekhā cānaṅgavegānaṅgāṅkuśāpi ca //
3.19.d:
अनङ्गमदनानङ्गमदनातुरया सह ।
अनङ्गलेखा चानङ्गवेगानङ्गाङ्कुशापि च ॥
3.19.m: Anaṅgamadanā, together with Anaṅgamadanāturā, / Anaṅgalekhā, Anaṅgavegā, Anaṅgāṅkuśā,

3.19.s:
anaṅgamāligyaparā etā devyo japātviṣaḥ /
ikṣucāpaṃ puṣpaśarānpuṣpakandukamutpalam //
3.19.d:
अनङ्गमालिग्यपरा एता देव्यो जपात्विषः ।
इक्षुचापं पुष्पशरान्पुष्पकन्दुकमुत्पलम् ॥
3.19.m: and the supreme Anaṅgamālinī. These goddesses have the luster of hibiscus flowers; / holding a sugarcane bow, flower arrows, a flower ball, and a blue lotus,

3.19.s:
bibhratyo 'dabhravikrāntiśālinyo lalitājñayā /
bhaṇḍāsuramabhikruddhāḥ prajvalantya iva sthitāḥ //
3.19.d:
बिभ्रत्यो ऽदभ्रविक्रान्तिशालिन्यो ललिताज्ञया ।
भण्डासुरमभिक्रुद्धाः प्रज्वलन्त्य इव स्थिताः ॥
3.19.m: endowed with immense prowess by Lalitā's command, / they stood as if blazing with rage against the demon Bhaṇḍa.

3.19.s:
atha cakrarathendrasya ṣaṣṭhaṃ parva samāśritāḥ /
sarvasaṃkṣobhiṇīmukhyāḥ sampradāyākhyayā yutāḥ //
3.19.d:
अथ चक्ररथेन्द्रस्य षष्ठं पर्व समाश्रिताः ।
सर्वसंक्षोभिणीमुख्याः सम्प्रदायाख्यया युताः ॥
3.19.m: Now, stationed on the sixth step of the foremost chariot-cakra / are those headed by Sarvasaṃkṣobhiṇī, designated by the name Sampradāya.

3.19.s:
veṇīkṛtakacastomāḥ siṃdūratilakojjvalāḥ /
atitīvrasvabhāvāśca kālānalasamatviṣaḥ //
3.19.d:
वेणीकृतकचस्तोमाः सिंदूरतिलकोज्ज्वलाः ।
अतितीव्रस्वभावाश्च कालानलसमत्विषः ॥
3.19.m: With masses of hair braided, radiant with red sindūra marks, / of exceedingly fierce disposition, having a luster like the fire of cosmic dissolution,

3.19.s:
vahnibāṇaṃ vahnicāpaṃ vahnirūpamasiṃ tathā /
vahnicakrākhyāphalakaṃ dadhānā dīptavigrahāḥ //
3.19.d:
वह्निबाणं वह्निचापं वह्निरूपमसिं तथा ।
वह्निचक्राख्याफलकं दधाना दीप्तविग्रहाः ॥
3.19.m: bearing an arrow of fire, a bow of fire, a sword of the nature of fire, / and a shield named fire-cakra, their bodies are radiant with light.

3.19.s:
asurendraṃ prati kruddhāḥ kāmabhasmasamudbhavāḥ /
ājñāśaktaya evaitā lalitāyā mahaujasaḥ //
3.19.d:
असुरेन्द्रं प्रति क्रुद्धाः कामभस्मसमुद्भवाः ।
आज्ञाशक्तय एवैता ललिताया महौजसः ॥
3.19.m: Enraged against the lord of demons, arisen from the ashes of Kāma, / these are indeed the command-Śaktis of Lalitā, possessing great splendor:

3.19.s:
sarvasaṃkṣobhiṇī caiva sarvavidrāviṇī tathā /
sarvākarṣaṇikā śaktiḥ sarvāhlādinikā tathā //
3.19.d:
सर्वसंक्षोभिणी चैव सर्वविद्राविणी तथा ।
सर्वाकर्षणिका शक्तिः सर्वाह्लादिनिका तथा ॥
3.19.m: Sarvasaṃkṣobhiṇī, Sarvavidrāviṇī, / the Śakti Sarvākarṣaṇikā, and Sarvāhlādinikā,

3.19.s:
sarvasaṃmohinīśaktiḥ sarvastambhanaśaktikā /
sarvajṛṃbhaṇaśaktiśca sarvonmādanaśaktikā //
3.19.d:
सर्वसंमोहिनीशक्तिः सर्वस्तम्भनशक्तिका ।
सर्वजृंभणशक्तिश्च सर्वोन्मादनशक्तिका ॥
3.19.m: the Śakti Sarvasaṃmohinī, the Śakti Sarvastambhanā, / the Śakti Sarvajṛmbhaṇā, and the Śakti Sarvonmādanā,

3.19.s:
sarvārthasādhikā śaktiḥ sarvasampattipūraṇī /
sarvamantramayī śaktiḥ sarvadvandvakṣayaṅkarī //
3.19.d:
सर्वार्थसाधिका शक्तिः सर्वसम्पत्तिपूरणी ।
सर्वमन्त्रमयी शक्तिः सर्वद्वन्द्वक्षयङ्करी ॥
3.19.m: the Śakti Sarvārthasādhikā, Sarvasampattipūraṇī, / the Śakti Sarvamantramayī, and Sarvadvandvakṣayaṅkarī.

3.19.s:
evaṃ tu sampradāyānāṃ nāmāni kathitāni vai /
atha pañcamaparvasthāḥ kulottīrṇā iti smṛtāḥ //
3.19.d:
एवं तु सम्प्रदायानां नामानि कथितानि वै ।
अथ पञ्चमपर्वस्थाः कुलोत्तीर्णा इति स्मृताः ॥
3.19.m: Thus indeed the names of the [yoginī] lineages have been spoken. / Now those situated on the fifth tier are known as the Kulottīrṇās.

3.19.s:
tāśca saptaṭikasaṅkāśāḥ paraśuṃ pāśameva ca /
gadāṃ ghaṇṭāṃ maṇiṃ caiva dadhānā dīptavigrahāḥ //
3.19.d:
ताश्च सप्तटिकसङ्काशाः परशुं पाशमेव च ।
गदां घण्टां मणिं चैव दधाना दीप्तविग्रहाः ॥
3.19.m: Resembling crystals, they bear a battle-axe and a noose, / a mace, a bell, and a jewel, their bodies blazing.

3.19.s:
devadviṣamati kruddhā bhrukuṭīkuṭilānanāḥ /
etāsāmapi nāmāni samākarmaya kumbhaja //
3.19.d:
देवद्विषमति क्रुद्धा भ्रुकुटीकुटिलाननाः ।
एतासामपि नामानि समाकर्मय कुम्भज ॥
3.19.m: Furious toward the enemies of the gods, their faces curved with knit brows: / hear also their names, O pot-born [Agastya]!

3.19.s:
sarvasiddhipradā devī sarvasampatpradā tathā /
sarvapriyaṅkarī devī sarvamaṅgalakāriṇī //
3.19.d:
सर्वसिद्धिप्रदा देवी सर्वसम्पत्प्रदा तथा ।
सर्वप्रियङ्करी देवी सर्वमङ्गलकारिणी ॥
3.19.m: The goddess Sarvasiddhipradā, and likewise Sarvasampatpradā, / the goddess Sarvapriyaṅkarī, Sarvamaṅgalakāriṇī,

3.19.s: sarvakāmapradā devī sarvaduḥkhavimocinī //
3.19.d: सर्वकामप्रदा देवी सर्वदुःखविमोचिनी ॥
3.19.m: the goddess Sarvakāmapradā, Sarvaduḥkhavimocinī,

3.19.s:
sarvamṛtyupraśaminī sarvavighnanivāriṇī /
sarvāṅgasundarī devī sarvasaubhāgyadāyinī //
3.19.d:
सर्वमृत्युप्रशमिनी सर्वविघ्ननिवारिणी ।
सर्वाङ्गसुन्दरी देवी सर्वसौभाग्यदायिनी ॥
3.19.m: Sarvamṛtyupraśaminī, Sarvavighnanivāriṇī, / the goddess Sarvāṅgasundarī, [and] Sarvasaubhāgyadāyinī.

3.19.s:
daśaintāḥ kathitā devyo dayayā pūritāśayāḥ /
cakre turīyaparvasthā muktāhārasamatviṣaḥ //
3.19.d:
दशैन्ताः कथिता देव्यो दयया पूरिताशयाः ।
चक्रे तुरीयपर्वस्था मुक्ताहारसमत्विषः ॥
3.19.m: These ten goddesses are spoken of, their hearts filled with compassion. / Situated on the fourth tier of the cakra, having the luster of pearl necklaces,

3.19.s:
nigarbhayoginīnāmnā prathitā daśa kīrtitāḥ /
sarvajñā sarvaśaktiśca sarvaiśvaryapradā tathā //
3.19.d:
निगर्भयोगिनीनाम्ना प्रथिता दश कीर्तिताः ।
सर्वज्ञा सर्वशक्तिश्च सर्वैश्वर्यप्रदा तथा ॥
3.19.m: ten are celebrated by the name Nigarbhayoginīs: / Sarvajñā, Sarvaśakti, and likewise Sarvaiśvaryapradā,

3.19.s:
sarvajñānamayī devī sarvavyādhivināśinī /
sarvādhārasvarūpā ca sarvapāpaharā tathā //
3.19.d:
सर्वज्ञानमयी देवी सर्वव्याधिविनाशिनी ।
सर्वाधारस्वरूपा च सर्वपापहरा तथा ॥
3.19.m: the goddess Sarvajñānamayī, Sarvavyādhivināśinī, / she who is Sarvādhārasvarūpā, and likewise Sarvapāpaharā,

3.19.s:
sarvānandamayī devī sarvarakṣāsvarūpiṇī /
daśamī devatājñeyā sarveṣsitaphalapradā //
3.19.d:
सर्वानन्दमयी देवी सर्वरक्षास्वरूपिणी ।
दशमी देवताज्ञेया सर्वेष्सितफलप्रदा ॥
3.19.m: the goddess Sarvānandamayī, Sarvarakṣāsvarūpiṇī; / the tenth deity should be known as Sarvepsitaphalapradā.

3.19.s:
etāścaturbhujā jñeyā vajraṃ śaktiṃ ca tomaram /
cakraṃ caivābhibibhrāṇā bhaṇḍāsuravadhodyatāḥ //
3.19.d:
एताश्चतुर्भुजा ज्ञेया वज्रं शक्तिं च तोमरम् ।
चक्रं चैवाभिबिभ्राणा भण्डासुरवधोद्यताः ॥
3.19.m: These should be known as four-armed, bearing a thunderbolt, a spear, a dart, / and a discus, ready for the slaying of the asura Bhaṇḍa.

3.19.s:
atha cakrarathendrasya tṛtīyaṃ parvasaṃśritāḥ /
rahasyayoginīnāmnā prakhyātā vāgadhīśvarāḥ //
3.19.d:
अथ चक्ररथेन्द्रस्य तृतीयं पर्वसंश्रिताः ।
रहस्ययोगिनीनाम्ना प्रख्याता वागधीश्वराः ॥
3.19.m: Now, stationed upon the third tier of the supreme chariot of the cakra, / celebrated by the name Rahasyayoginīs, are the presiding deities of speech.

3.19.s:
raktāśokaprasūnābhābāṇakārmukapāṇayaḥ /
kavacacchannasarvāṅgayo vīṇāpustakaśobhitāḥ //
3.19.d:
रक्ताशोकप्रसूनाभाबाणकार्मुकपाणयः ।
कवचच्छन्नसर्वाङ्गयो वीणापुस्तकशोभिताः ॥
3.19.m: Having the luster of red Aśoka blossoms, holding arrows and bows in their hands, / their whole bodies covered in armor, adorned with vīṇās and books:

3.19.s:
vaśinī caiva kāmeśī bhoginī vimalā tathā /
aruṇāca javinyākhyā sarveśī kaulinī tathā //
3.19.d:
वशिनी चैव कामेशी भोगिनी विमला तथा ।
अरुणाच जविन्याख्या सर्वेशी कौलिनी तथा ॥
3.19.m: Vaśinī, Kāmeśī, Bhoginī, and likewise Vimalā, / Aruṇā, the one named Javinī, Sarveśī, and likewise Kaulinī.

3.19.s:
aṣṭāvetāḥ smṛtā devyo daityasaṃhārahetavaḥ /
atha cakrarathendrasya dvitīyaṃ parvasaṃśritāḥ //
3.19.d:
अष्टावेताः स्मृता देव्यो दैत्यसंहारहेतवः ।
अथ चक्ररथेन्द्रस्य द्वितीयं पर्वसंश्रिताः ॥
3.19.m: These eight goddesses are remembered as the cause of the destruction of the Daityas. / Now, stationed upon the second tier of the supreme chariot of the cakra,

3.19.s:
cāpabāṇau pānapātraṃ māturuṅgaṃ kṛpāṇikām /
tisrastripīṭhanilayā aṣṭabāhusamanvitāḥ //
3.19.d:
चापबाणौ पानपात्रं मातुरुङ्गं कृपाणिकाम् ।
तिस्रस्त्रिपीठनिलया अष्टबाहुसमन्विताः ॥
3.19.m: holding bow and arrow, a drinking cup, a citron fruit, and a dagger, / three [goddesses] dwell in the three pīṭhas, endowed with eight arms;

3.19.s:
palakaṃ nāgapāśaṃ ca ghaṇṭāṃ caiva mahādhvanim /
vibhrāṇā madirāmattā atiguptarahasyakāḥ //
3.19.d:
पलकं नागपाशं च घण्टां चैव महाध्वनिम् ।
विभ्राणा मदिरामत्ता अतिगुप्तरहस्यकाः ॥
3.19.m: holding a shield, a serpent-noose, and a bell of great sound, / intoxicated with wine, [they are] the most secret and esoteric ones:

3.19.s:
kāmeśī caiva vajreśī bhagamālinyathāparā /
tisra etāḥ smṛtā devyo bhaṇḍe kopasamanvitāḥ //
3.19.d:
कामेशी चैव वज्रेशी भगमालिन्यथापरा ।
तिस्र एताः स्मृता देव्यो भण्डे कोपसमन्विताः ॥
3.19.m: Kāmeśī, Vajreśī, and then the other, Bhagamālinī. / These three goddesses are remembered, filled with wrath toward Bhaṇḍa,

3.19.s:
lalitāsamamāhātmyā lalitāsamatejasaḥ /
etāstu nityaṃ śrīdevyā antaraṅgāḥ prakīrtitāḥ //
3.19.d:
ललितासममाहात्म्या ललितासमतेजसः ।
एतास्तु नित्यं श्रीदेव्या अन्तरङ्गाः प्रकीर्तिताः ॥
3.19.m: possessing majesty equal to Lalitā, possessing splendor equal to Lalitā. / These are celebrated as the intimate companions of the auspicious Goddess at all times.

3.19.s:
athānandamahāpīṭhe rathamadhyamaparvaṇi /
parito racitāvāsāḥ proktāḥ pañcadaśākṣarāḥ //
3.19.d:
अथानन्दमहापीठे रथमध्यमपर्वणि ।
परितो रचितावासाः प्रोक्ताः पञ्चदशाक्षराः ॥
3.19.m: Now, upon the great pīṭha of bliss, on the central tier of the chariot, / with residences arranged all around, are spoken the fifteen-syllabled ones,

3.19.s:
tithinityāḥ kālarūpā viśvaṃ vyāpyaiva saṃsthitāḥ /
bhaṇḍāsurādidaityeṣu prakṣubdhabhrukuṭītaṭāḥ //
3.19.d:
तिथिनित्याः कालरूपा विश्वं व्याप्यैव संस्थिताः ।
भण्डासुरादिदैत्येषु प्रक्षुब्धभ्रुकुटीतटाः ॥
3.19.m: the Nityās of the lunar days, who are forms of time, abiding pervading the entire universe, / their knit brows trembling with fury against the Daityas headed by the asura Bhaṇḍa,

3.19.s:
devīsamanijākārā devīsamanijāyudhāḥ /
jagatāmupakārāya vartamānā yugeyuge //
3.19.d:
देवीसमनिजाकारा देवीसमनिजायुधाः ।
जगतामुपकाराय वर्तमाना युगेयुगे ॥
3.19.m: having forms equal to the Goddess, having weapons equal to the Goddess, / operating age after age for the welfare of the worlds.

3.19.s:
tāsāṃ nāmāni mattastvamavadhārayakumbhaja /
kāmeśī bhagamālā ca nityaklinnā tathaiva ca //
3.19.d:
तासां नामानि मत्तस्त्वमवधारयकुम्भज ।
कामेशी भगमाला च नित्यक्लिन्ना तथैव च ॥
3.19.m: Learn their names from me, O pot-born [Agastya]: / Kāmeśī, Bhagamālā, and likewise Nityaklinnā,

3.19.s:
bheruṇḍā vahnivāsinyo mahāvajreśvarī tathā /
datī ca tvaritā devī navamī kulasundarī //
3.19.d:
भेरुण्डा वह्निवासिन्यो महावज्रेश्वरी तथा ।
दती च त्वरिता देवी नवमी कुलसुन्दरी ॥
3.19.m: Bheruṇḍā, Vahnivāsinī, and Mahāvajreśvarī, / Dūtī, the goddess Tvaritā, the ninth Kulasundarī,

3.19.s:
nityā nīlapatākā ca vijayā sarvamaṅgalā /
jvālāmālinikācitre daśa pañca ca kīrtitāḥ //
3.19.d:
नित्या नीलपताका च विजया सर्वमङ्गला ।
ज्वालामालिनिकाचित्रे दश पञ्च च कीर्तिताः ॥
3.19.m: Nityā, Nīlapatākā, Vijayā, Sarvamaṅgalā, / Jvālāmālinī, and Citrā: thus fifteen are celebrated.

3.19.s:
etābhiḥ sahitā devī sadā sevaikabuddhibhiḥ /
duṣṭaṃ bhaṇḍāsuraṃ jetuṃ niryayau parameśvarī //
3.19.d:
एताभिः सहिता देवी सदा सेवैकबुद्धिभिः ।
दुष्टं भण्डासुरं जेतुं निर्ययौ परमेश्वरी ॥
3.19.m: Accompanied by these, whose minds are always single-pointed in service, / the Supreme Goddess set forth to conquer the evil asura Bhaṇḍa.

3.19.s:
mantrināthā mahācakre gītiṃ cakre rathottame /
saptaparvāṇi coktāni tatra devyāśca tāḥ śṛṇu //
3.19.d:
मन्त्रिनाथा महाचक्रे गीतिं चक्रे रथोत्तमे ।
सप्तपर्वाणि चोक्तानि तत्र देव्याश्च ताः शृणु ॥
3.19.m: The sovereign Mantriṇī is in the great cakra, the supreme chariot named Geyacakra. / Seven tiers are declared there; hear of those goddesses belonging to her:

3.19.s:
geyacakrarathe parvamadhyapīḍhaniketanā /
saṃgītayoginī proktā śrīdevyā ativallabhā //
3.19.d:
गेयचक्ररथे पर्वमध्यपीढनिकेतना ।
संगीतयोगिनी प्रोक्ता श्रीदेव्या अतिवल्लभा ॥
3.19.m: In the Geyacakra chariot, having her abode in the central pīṭha of the tier, / Saṃgītayoginī is spoken of, dearly beloved of the auspicious Goddess.

3.19.s:
tadeva prathamaṃ parva mantriṇyāstu nivāsabhūḥ /
atha dvitīyaparvasthā geyacakre rathottame //
3.19.d:
तदेव प्रथमं पर्व मन्त्रिण्यास्तु निवासभूः ।
अथ द्वितीयपर्वस्था गेयचक्रे रथोत्तमे ॥
3.19.m: That very first tier is the dwelling place of Mantriṇī. / Now, stationed upon the second tier in the supreme Geyacakra chariot,

3.19.s:
ratiḥ prītirmanojā ca vīṇākārmukapāṇayaḥ /
tamālaśyāmalākārā dānavonmūlanakṣamāḥ //
3.19.d:
रतिः प्रीतिर्मनोजा च वीणाकार्मुकपाणयः ।
तमालश्यामलाकारा दानवोन्मूलनक्षमाः ॥
3.19.m: are Rati, Prīti, and Manojā, holding vīṇās and bows in hand, / dark like tamāla trees in appearance, capable of uprooting the Dānavas.

3.19.s:
tṛtīyaparvasaṃrūḍhā manobhūbāṇadevatā /
drāviṇī śoṣiṇī caiva bandhinī mohinī tathā //
3.19.d:
तृतीयपर्वसंरूढा मनोभूबाणदेवता ।
द्राविणी शोषिणी चैव बन्धिनी मोहिनी तथा ॥
3.19.m: Mounted upon the third tier are the deities of the arrows of the mind-born [Kāma]: / Drāviṇī, Śoṣiṇī, Bandhinī, Mohinī,

3.19.s:
unmādinīti pañcaitā dīptakārmukapāṇayaḥ /
tatra parvaṇyadhastāttu vartamānā mahaujasaḥ //
3.19.d:
उन्मादिनीति पञ्चैता दीप्तकार्मुकपाणयः ।
तत्र पर्वण्यधस्तात्तु वर्तमाना महौजसः ॥
3.19.m: and Unmādinī: these five, holding blazing bows in hand. / Stationed directly below on that tier are the ones of great splendor:

3.19.s:
kāmarājaśca kandarpauṃ manmatho makaradhvajaḥ /
manobhavaḥ pañcamaḥ syādete trailokyamohanāḥ //
3.19.d:
कामराजश्च कन्दर्पौं मन्मथो मकरध्वजः ।
मनोभवः पञ्चमः स्यादेते त्रैलोक्यमोहनाः ॥
3.19.m: Kāmarāja, Kandarpa, Manmatha, Makaradhvaja, / and Manobhava is the fifth: these bewitch the three worlds.

3.19.s:
kastūrītilakollāsibhālāmuktāvirājitāḥ /
kavacacchannasarvāṅgāḥ palāśaprasavatviṣaḥ //
3.19.d:
कस्तूरीतिलकोल्लासिभालामुक्ताविराजिताः ।
कवचच्छन्नसर्वाङ्गाः पलाशप्रसवत्विषः ॥
3.19.m: Their foreheads shine with musk marks, adorned with pearls, / all their limbs covered in armor, possessing the luster of palāśa blossoms,

3.19.s:
pañcakāmā ime proktā bhaṇḍāsuravadhārthinaḥ /
jeyacakrarathendrasya caturthaṃ parva saṃśritāḥ //
3.19.d:
पञ्चकामा इमे प्रोक्ता भण्डासुरवधार्थिनः ।
जेयचक्ररथेन्द्रस्य चतुर्थं पर्व संश्रिताः ॥
3.19.m: these Five Kāmas are declared, intent upon the slaying of the asura Bhaṇḍa. / Stationed on the fourth tier of the supreme chariot Geyacakra

3.19.s:
brahmīmukhyāstu pūrvoktāścaṇḍikā tvaṣṭamī parā /
tatra parvaṇyadhastācca lakṣmīścaiva sarasvatī //
3.19.d:
ब्रह्मीमुख्यास्तु पूर्वोक्ताश्चण्डिका त्वष्टमी परा ।
तत्र पर्वण्यधस्ताच्च लक्ष्मीश्चैव सरस्वती ॥
